searchDocs.content: System	Client	Shared	ServerPlacement	PlacementClient — preview + request	PlacementSystem — validation logic	PlacementServer — anti-exploit + finalize Stamina / Sprint	SprintController — predict drain/regen, FOV	SprintValidation — shared helpers	StaminaManager — authority, 10 Hz sync Junk	JunkController — pooled render + ropes	GenericPoolInstance/Object	JunkService — spawn + collection auth Grabhook	Tool script — raycast + visuals	—	Server script — validate + award Shredder	ShredderClient — prompts + handshake	ShredderMath, ShredderResultCodes	ShredderServer — validate + eject Health	HealthController, HUD	—	HealthManager — regen + sync Sound	SoundController bootstraps SoundManager	SoundManager, SoundConfig	ReplicatedSoundService relay Camera	CameraController, CameraBoomController	—	— Notifications	NotificationController renders toasts	NotificationManager, NotificationConfig	—

searchDocs.title: Communication Diagram​
searchDocs.content: ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ CLIENT │ │ │ │ Controllers ──[Signals]──> other Controllers / UI │ │ │ │ │ │ fire Packet request │ │ ▼ │ │ ┌─────────────────────────┐ │ │ │ Packets layer │ ◄── typed; no raw Remotes │ │ └────────────┬────────────┘ │ └───────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ RemoteEvent / RemoteFunction (internal) ┌───────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ ▼ │ │ ┌─────────────────────────┐ │ │ │ Packets layer │ │ │ └────────────┬────────────┘ │ │ │ sync / response Packet │ │ ▼ │ │ Authority Modules (StaminaManager, PlacementServer, …) │ │ │ │ SERVER │ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   Signals are client-only and in-process — they never cross the network. All cross-boundary traffic uses Packets.

searchDocs.title: Where Content Lives​
searchDocs.content: There are two sources of documentation:  Narrative pages (docs/) — the files you are reading now. Written by hand in Markdown and checked into this repository. Covers architecture, playbooks, getting-started guides, and everything that isn't a raw API reference.API reference — generated automatically by Moonwave from doc-comments (--[=[...]=] blocks) in the Luau source under src/. Moonwave extracts these at build time; no separate documentation file is needed for module APIs.

searchDocs.title: Local Preview​
searchDocs.content: Install Moonwave globally once:  npm i -g moonwave@latest   Then, from the repo root:  Command	Effectmoonwave dev	Starts a live-reload local server. Edit any docs/ page or source doc-comment and the browser updates instantly. moonwave build	Produces a static output in build/ for inspection. The CI pipeline runs this automatically — you rarely need it locally.

searchDocs.title: Publishing​
searchDocs.content: Pushing to main triggers a GitHub Action that:  Runs moonwave build.Pushes the static output to the separate endless-journey-docs repository.GitHub Pages serves the result from that repo.  You do not need to run the build or push to endless-journey-docs manually.

searchDocs.title: The Discipline Rule​
searchDocs.content: When a code change touches a system, the same commit must also update:  That system's narrative page under docs/.Any affected playbook in docs/playbooks/.The networking map or signals map if a new packet or signal was added.  This extends the project's existing "record any new signal/packet" rule (see old guide § Recommended Update Process) to cover the Moonwave site. Keeping documentation and code in the same commit makes it easy to find the change context later and prevents the docs from silently drifting out of date.  tip If the change is large (e.g. a new system), write the narrative page first as a draft, then implement the code, then finalize both in the closing commit. This forces you to articulate the design before you are buried in implementation details.

searchDocs.title: Initial Setup​
searchDocs.content: After cloning the repo, run this once:  rokit install   This installs the pinned versions of Rojo, Wally, wally-package-types, and selene into your local toolchain.

searchDocs.title: Common Commands​
searchDocs.content: Command	Purposerojo serve	Start the live-sync server for Studio editing. rojo build -o "Game Instance.rbxlx"	Emit a static place file from src/. rojo sourcemap default.project.json -o sourcemap.json --include-non-scripts	Regenerate the sourcemap used by Luau LSP. Re-run after adding or moving files. wally install	Fetch Wally dependencies into Packages/ (shared) and ServerPackages/ (server). wally-package-types --sourcemap sourcemap.json Packages/	Regenerate type exports for Wally packages. Run after every wally install so Luau type-checking sees package types. selene src	Lint Luau source against the Roblox standard library (std = "roblox", config in selene.toml).

searchDocs.title: After wally install — Manual Studio Step Required​
searchDocs.content: TweenPlus TweenPreallocations After every wally install, you must manually re-set the TweenPreallocations attribute in Studio — or TweenPlus will crash on load. wally install deletes and regenerates the entire Packages/ directory. The TweenPlus package (Packages/_Index/alexanderlindholt_tweenplus@<ver>/tweenplus) reads a TweenPreallocations number attribute from its own script instance at require-time with no nil fallback (table.create(script.Parent:GetAttribute("TweenPreallocations"))). When the attribute is absent the package throws: invalid argument #1 to 'create' (number expected, got nil) This error cascades: TweenPlus → PlacementSystem → SprintController → every consumer fails to load. Steps to fix after wally install: Open Studio with rojo serve running.In the Explorer, navigate to:ReplicatedStorage → Packages → _Index → alexanderlindholt_tweenplus@<ver> → tweenplusIn the Properties panel, add an attribute: Name: TweenPreallocationsType: numberValue: 256 Save the place file. The attribute persists until the next wally install.  A default.project.json $properties override cannot be used here: in live Rojo sync, Rojo recreates the path-synced instance instead of patching it, so the attribute would be wiped on every sync cycle.

searchDocs.title: No Automated Tests​
searchDocs.content: note There is no automated test suite. All verification happens by playtesting in Studio. See the How-To Playbooks for the manual smoke-test steps specific to each system.

searchDocs.title: Core Systems​
searchDocs.content: System	What it doesPlacement	Grid and free-placement of world objects; client previews, server validates. Stamina / Sprint	Server-authoritative stamina with client-side prediction for smooth feel. Junk	Server spawns weighted floating junk; client renders pooled visuals. Grabhook	Tool-driven traversal; client drives visuals and raycast, server awards. Shredder	Two-step proximity interaction that converts junk into craft materials. Health	Server-authoritative regen and sync; client drives the HUD bar. Train Fuel	Global fuel economy; players feed Energy junk at the engine to keep the train running. Camera	Unified third-person + aim modes with MotionMaster spring transitions. Sound	SoundManager is the single entry point for all client audio; positional SFX replicate via the server relay. Notifications	Toast stack for refuel errors and other player-facing feedback.

searchDocs.title: Design Philosophy​
searchDocs.content: Every gameplay system follows a client predicts / server authoritative pattern with a shared validator. The client runs local prediction (placement preview, stamina drain, fuel bar interpolation) so interaction feels instant, while the server re-validates every request and broadcasts the authoritative result. Protocol changes must go through src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Packets/init.luau; cross-module events go through src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Signals/init.luau. When in doubt, the server wins.

searchDocs.title: How to Read These Docs​
searchDocs.content: Getting Started — install the toolchain, run a build, and understand the one manual step that trips everyone up (TweenPreallocations).Architecture — runtime layers, cross-cutting modules, and the authority pattern.Systems — one page per core system (placement, stamina, junk, grabhook, shredder, health, train fuel, camera, sound, notifications).How-To Playbooks — step-by-step safe-change guides (add a placeable, tune stamina, adjust junk flow, etc.).Reference — the networking / signals / config maps, Janitor and MotionMaster cheat-sheets, plus the Moonwave-generated API docs for every annotated module.

searchDocs.title: 1. Choose a notification type​
searchDocs.content: The canonical types are defined in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/NotificationConfig.luau:  "success" | "info" | "warn" | "alert" | "default"   Each type has a pre-configured background color (NotificationConfig.Colors), icon image (NotificationConfig.ImageIds), and stinger SFX (NotificationConfig.SfxNames). If an existing type fits, skip to step 3.

searchDocs.title: 2. (Optional) Add a new type​
searchDocs.content: If none of the five built-in types fit, extend NotificationConfig:  File: src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/NotificationConfig.luau  Add the new lowercase key to every relevant table:  -- 1. Register the type name NotificationConfig.Types = { "success", "info", "warn", "alert", "default", "mytype" } -- 2. Background color NotificationConfig.Colors.mytype = Color3.fromRGB(80, 40, 120) -- 3. Background transparency (0 = opaque, 1 = invisible) NotificationConfig.BaseTransparency.mytype = 0.5 -- 4. Icon asset ID NotificationConfig.ImageIds.mytype = "rbxassetid://XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX" -- 5. SFX stinger — must match a key in SoundConfig.Sfx NotificationConfig.SfxNames.mytype = "NotifDefault"   If you add a custom stinger, first register it in SoundConfig.Sfx (see Add a Sound).

searchDocs.title: 3. Fire the signal from any client controller​
searchDocs.content: local Signals = require(ReplicatedStorage.SharedModules.Signals) -- Basic timed toast (disappears after the default duration): Signals.RequestNotification:Fire("success", "Item placed!") -- Custom duration (seconds): Signals.RequestNotification:Fire("warn", "Low fuel!", 5) -- Executed-function toast (stays until the function returns, then closes): Signals.RequestNotification:Fire("info", "Loading...", nil, function() -- async work here; toast closes when this returns task.wait(2) end) -- Dismiss all active toasts: Signals.RequestClearNotifications:Fire()   Signal signature (from src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Signals/init.luau):  RequestNotification : Signal<string, string, number?, (() -> ())?> arg1 notificationType (lowercase, must be in NotificationConfig.Types) arg2 message (display text, wraps automatically) arg3 duration? (seconds; nil = config default per device) arg4 executedFunction? (if provided, toast stays until function returns)   The stack allows up to NotificationConfig.MaxConcurrent (default 5) concurrent toasts. When the cap is exceeded the oldest non-executed toast is automatically closed.

searchDocs.title: Verify in Studio​
searchDocs.content: Play-test in Studio (client context).Trigger the code path that fires Signals.RequestNotification.Confirm the toast appears at the top of the screen, plays its stinger, and auto-dismisses after the expected duration.If the toast does not appear: confirm the type string is lowercase and present in NotificationConfig.Types; confirm NotificationController.client.luau has run NotificationManager.Init().    See also: Notification system reference

searchDocs.title: Add a Network Packet (Client ↔ Server Channel)
Checklist​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Add a Network Packet (Client ↔ Server Channel)

searchDocs.title: 1. Open Packets/init.luau​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Add a Network Packet (Client ↔ Server Channel)
searchDocs.content: File: src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Packets/init.luau  Browse the existing definitions to understand the declaration style before adding yours.

searchDocs.title: 2. Declare the packet​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Add a Network Packet (Client ↔ Server Channel)
searchDocs.content: Add your packet in the appropriate section (or create a new labelled section). Match the style of existing entries: a local variable, a direction comment, and field-level type annotations.  Simple payload (no response):  -- Client → Server: description of what this carries local MyPacket = Packet( "MyPacket", Packet.String, -- fieldOne Packet.NumberF32, -- fieldTwo Packet.Boolean8 -- fieldThree )   Request/response pattern:  -- Client → Server: description local ReqMyAction = Packet( "ReqMyAction", Packet.Instance -- target ):Response( Packet.Boolean8, -- success Packet.NumberU8 -- reason code )   Server → Client broadcast:  -- Server → All Clients: description local BroadcastMyEvent = Packet( "BroadcastMyEvent", Packet.Instance :: Player, -- the relevant player Packet.Vector3F32 -- position )   Available type tokens: Packet.String, Packet.Boolean8, Packet.NumberF32, Packet.NumberF64, Packet.NumberU8, Packet.NumberU16, Packet.NumberF16, Packet.Instance, Packet.Vector3F32, Packet.CFrameF32U16, Packet.Any.  For high-frequency unreliable streams (e.g., per-frame position updates) use the makeUnreliable helper already present in the file.

searchDocs.title: 3. Export the packet​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Add a Network Packet (Client ↔ Server Channel)
searchDocs.content: Add it to the return table at the bottom of init.luau:  return { -- ... existing entries ... MyPacket = MyPacket, ReqMyAction = ReqMyAction, BroadcastMyEvent = BroadcastMyEvent, }

searchDocs.title: 4. Wire the sender​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Add a Network Packet (Client ↔ Server Channel)
searchDocs.content: On the client (fires to server):  local Packets = require(ReplicatedStorage.SharedModules.Packets) -- Fire and forget: Packets.MyPacket:Fire(valueOne, valueTwo, valueThree) -- Request/response: local success, reasonCode = Packets.ReqMyAction:Fire(targetInstance)   On the server (fires to clients):  local Packets = require(ReplicatedStorage.SharedModules.Packets) -- Broadcast to all: Packets.BroadcastMyEvent:Fire(player, position) -- Fire to one client: Packets.BroadcastMyEvent:FireClient(targetPlayer, player, position)

searchDocs.title: 5. Wire the receiver​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Add a Network Packet (Client ↔ Server Channel)
searchDocs.content: On the server (listening for client sends):  Packets.MyPacket.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(sender: Player, valueOne, valueTwo, valueThree) -- validate and handle end)   On the client (listening for server sends):  Packets.BroadcastMyEvent.OnClientEvent:Connect(function(player, position) -- handle end)

searchDocs.title: 6. Update the networking map​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Add a Network Packet (Client ↔ Server Channel)
searchDocs.content: Open docs/reference/networking-map.md and add a row for your new packet in the same commit. Include: packet name, direction (C→S / S→C / S→All), payload summary, and which scripts send/receive it.

searchDocs.title: Verify in Studio​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Add a Network Packet (Client ↔ Server Channel)
searchDocs.content: Play-test with at least one client and the server running.Trigger the send path and confirm the receiver fires.Check the Output window — Packet will warn if a type mismatch or serialization error occurs.For request/response packets, confirm the response values arrive correctly on the caller side.    See also: Networking map reference

searchDocs.title: Steps​
searchDocs.content: Author the model in Studio.Open Studio and build or import the item as a Model. Give it a clear, unique name (e.g. WoodenCrate). This name is the canonical identifier shared between the storage folder and the PlaceableName attribute. Place the model in the placeable-items storage folder.Move (or keep) the model inside the storage location that PlacementServer scans at startup. Verify src/ServerScriptService/PlacementServer.server.luau for the exact FindFirstChild / WaitForChild call that resolves the folder name, and make sure your model lands there. Add a CollisionBox part.Inside the model, create a BasePart named CollisionBox. Size and position it to represent the footprint used for overlap/validity checks. Set Anchored = true, CanCollide = false, and make it invisible (Transparency = 1). PlacementSystem reads this part to decide valid placement. Set the PlaceableName attribute on the Tool.On the Tool instance that players use to enter placement mode, open Properties → Attributes and add a string attribute named PlaceableName with the value matching the model name from step 1 (e.g. WoodenCrate). PlacementServer reads this attribute at line 205 and PlacementClient at line 253. Configure ghost appearance (optional).Ghost transparency and color cues come from src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/PlacementConfig.luau. Relevant fields: VisualGhostTransparency — opacity of the main model parts during previewCollisionBoxGhostTransparency — opacity of CollisionBox while ghostingColorValid / ColorInvalid — tint applied to the ghostShowCollisionBox — set true temporarily to debug footprint alignment Test grid mode and free mode.In a live Studio session (Rojo serving), equip the tool, open build mode, and place the item in both grid-snapped and free-rotation modes. Confirm the ghost tracks the cursor correctly and snaps as expected. Validate multiplayer ghost behavior.Run a local server with at least two clients. Confirm that observers see the ghost rendered correctly (via the replication path in PlacementClient) and that the server accepts the final placement without a distance/raycast rejection from PlacementServer. If you also need Stash / Move support, see Enable Stash & Move for the additional attribute and server wiring.

searchDocs.title: Verify in Studio​
searchDocs.content: Equip the new Tool, enter build mode, and place the item. Check the Output window for any PlacementServer rejection messages. Then have a second client observe: the placed item should appear at the confirmed position with no ghost artifact remaining.    See also: Placement system

searchDocs.title: 1. Open Signals/init.luau​
searchDocs.content: File: src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Signals/init.luau  Browse existing entries to understand the declaration style and grouping before adding yours.

searchDocs.title: 2. Add your signal​
searchDocs.content: Add the signal under the relevant comment group (or add a new group). Follow the existing pattern exactly — type-annotate the generic parameter so Luau can check call sites:  -- My System (Client Side) -- Fired by <ProducerScript> when <event>. Consumed by <ConsumerScript>. -- (<argOne>: type, <argTwo>: type) MySignal = Signal() :: Signal.Signal<string, number>,   For signals with no payload (fire/connect only):  MySignal = Signal(),

searchDocs.title: 3. Fire from the producer​
searchDocs.content: local Signals = require(ReplicatedStorage.SharedModules.Signals) Signals.MySignal:Fire("hello", 42)   Only one script should act as the authoritative producer. Document it in the signal's comment.

searchDocs.title: 4. Connect in the consumer(s)​
searchDocs.content: local Signals = require(ReplicatedStorage.SharedModules.Signals) Signals.MySignal:Connect(function(argOne: string, argTwo: number) -- handle the event end)   When the consumer has a scoped lifecycle (e.g., a GUI controller), track the connection with a Janitor so it is disconnected on cleanup:  cleaner:Add(Signals.MySignal:Connect(function(argOne, argTwo) -- handle end), "Disconnect")

searchDocs.title: 5. Update the signals map​
searchDocs.content: Open docs/reference/signals-map.md and add a row for your new signal in the same commit. Include: signal name, producer script, consumer script(s), and a one-line purpose summary.

searchDocs.title: Verify in Studio​
searchDocs.content: Play-test in Studio.Trigger the code path that fires the signal.Confirm the consumer callback runs with the expected arguments.If the consumer never fires: confirm both scripts require the same Signals module instance (both via ReplicatedStorage.SharedModules.Signals) and that the consumer connects before the first fire.    See also: Signals map reference

searchDocs.title: 1. Open SoundConfig​
searchDocs.content: File: src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/SoundConfig.luau  The config exports three tables: SoundConfig.Sfx, SoundConfig.Music.Playlists, and SoundConfig.Ambience.Beds.

searchDocs.title: 2. Add your definition​
searchDocs.content: One-shot / looped SFX — add an entry to SoundConfig.Sfx:  MyNewSfx = { Id = "rbxassetid://XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX", Volume = 0.5, -- optional; default engine volume if omitted Pitch = 1.0, -- optional PitchRange = { 0.9, 1.1 }, -- optional; overrides Pitch; random per play Group = "SFX", -- "SFX" | "BGM" | "Ambience"; default "SFX" Replicate = true, -- set true only for positional sounds other clients should hear Debounce = 0.1, -- optional; min seconds between plays (anti-spam) PoolInitial = 2, -- optional; for PlaySFXAt only — pre-warms the pool at Init PoolMax = 8, -- optional; hard cap for the positional pool },   The SoundDef type (exported from SoundConfig) documents every field.  Music track — add asset IDs to one of the three context playlists in SoundConfig.Music.Playlists (see BGM contexts below):  Normal = { Tracks = { "rbxassetid://AAA", "rbxassetid://BBB" }, Shuffle = true, FadeIn = 1.5, FadeOut = 1.5, GapMin = 60, GapMax = 300, Volume = 0.6, },   Ambience bed — add to SoundConfig.Ambience.Beds and, if it should start automatically, add its name to SoundConfig.Ambience.Autostart:  Beds = { MyAmbience = { Id = "rbxassetid://XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX", Volume = 0.4 }, }, Autostart = { "MyAmbience" }, -- fade in on SoundManager.Init()

searchDocs.title: 3. Play the sound from a client script​
searchDocs.content: Require SoundManager (never instantiate a Sound directly):  local SoundManager = require(ReplicatedStorage.SharedModules.SoundManager) -- One-shot 2D: SoundManager.PlaySFX("MyNewSfx") -- Positional (requires PoolInitial / PoolMax in the def for pre-warm): SoundManager.PlaySFXAt("MyNewSfx", somePosition) -- Looped SFX (returns a LoopHandle — call :Stop() to end it): local handle = SoundManager.PlayLooped("MyNewSfx") -- ...later: handle:Stop() -- Music playlist (normally driven by MusicDirector via context, not called directly): SoundManager.PlayMusic("Normal") -- Ambience (replaces current beds; use AddAmbience to layer): SoundManager.SetAmbience({ "MyAmbience" }) SoundManager.AddAmbience("MyAmbience") SoundManager.RemoveAmbience("MyAmbience") SoundManager.StopAmbience() -- Volume bus (0..1): SoundManager.SetVolume("SFX", 0.8)   SoundManager.Init() is called once by SoundController.client.luau — do not call it from feature code.

searchDocs.title: 4. Replication (positional broadcast)​
searchDocs.content: If other clients need to hear the sound when it plays at a world position, set Replicate = true in the SoundConfig.Sfx entry. The server relay uses SoundConfig.GetReplicatedIds() to build its allowlist. SoundConfig.GetPreloadIds() collects all non-empty IDs for ContentProvider:PreloadAsync.

searchDocs.title: BGM contexts​
searchDocs.content: Background music is context-driven, not played by name from feature code. MusicDirector.client.luau owns the active context and calls SoundManager.PlayMusic for you — you only ever add tracks to a playlist and (for combat) call the server API.

searchDocs.title: The three playlists​
searchDocs.content: SoundConfig.Music.Playlists has exactly three entries, one per context:  Context	Trigger	Gap behaviorNormal	Default; nothing else active	Gapped — random silence between tracks Combat	Server calls MusicService.SetContext(player, "Combat")	Continuous — overlapping crossfade, no silence LowFuel	Automatic, client-derived (see below)	Continuous — overlapping crossfade, no silence  Priority when more than one condition is true: Combat > LowFuel > Normal.

searchDocs.title: Adding tracks per context​
searchDocs.content: Add asset IDs to Tracks on the relevant playlist — do not add new playlist names, the engine and director both assume exactly these three:  Playlists = { Normal = { Tracks = { "rbxassetid://AAA", "rbxassetid://BBB" }, Shuffle = true, FadeIn = 1.5, FadeOut = 1.5, GapMin = 60, GapMax = 300, Volume = 0.6 }, Combat = { Tracks = { "rbxassetid://CCC" }, Shuffle = true, FadeIn = 1.0, FadeOut = 1.0, GapMin = 0, GapMax = 0, Volume = 0.7 }, LowFuel = { Tracks = { "rbxassetid://DDD" }, Shuffle = true, FadeIn = 2.0, FadeOut = 2.0, GapMin = 0, GapMax = 0, Volume = 0.55 }, }

searchDocs.title: Gap / fade fields​
searchDocs.content: Field	MeaningFadeIn	Seconds to fade the new track up from 0 at start FadeOut	Seconds to fade a track down to 0 at its end (or used as the crossfade overlap window when continuous) GapMin / GapMax	Random silence range (seconds) between tracks. GapMax <= 0 means continuous — the next track starts FadeOut seconds before the current one ends, producing an overlapping crossfade instead of silence Volume	Target playback volume for tracks in this playlist (pre-bus-volume)  Normal uses GapMin = 60, GapMax = 300 (a real silent gap between tracks). Combat and LowFuel use GapMin = 0, GapMax = 0 so they loop continuously with no silence.

searchDocs.title: Driving combat from server gameplay code​
searchDocs.content: Low fuel is automatic — never set it manually. Combat is the only context gameplay code drives, via the server-authoritative MusicService:  local MusicService = require(game.ServerStorage.SharedModules.MusicService) MusicService.SetContext(player, "Combat") -- on event/outpost enter MusicService.SetContext(player, "Normal") -- on event/outpost leave   SetContext fires the Packets.SetMusicContext packet to that one player; MusicDirector.client.luau receives it and resolves the active context by priority. Passing "Normal" clears the combat override — the client then falls back to LowFuel or Normal based on its own fuel state; it does not force Normal if fuel is still low.  Low fuel itself needs no code: MusicDirector watches Signals.OnTrainStateChanged and activates the LowFuel context whenever fuel / TrainConfig.MAX_FUEL drops below SoundConfig.Music.LowFuelPct (default 0.25).

searchDocs.title: Verify in Studio​
searchDocs.content: Play-test in Studio (client context).Trigger the code path that calls PlaySFX / PlaySFXAt / etc.Confirm the sound plays. If silent: check the asset ID is correct, that Volume is not 0, and that the Group bus volume (SoundManager.GetVolume) is non-zero.For positional sounds with Replicate = true, check the Output window for server-relay errors.For BGM: confirm the track plays in Normal by default, that calling MusicService.SetContext(player, "Combat") from a server script switches it with a crossfade (no silence), and that draining fuel below SoundConfig.Music.LowFuelPct switches to LowFuel when not in combat.    See also: SoundManager system reference

searchDocs.title: Steps​
searchDocs.content: Open the junk config.All tunable constants live in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/JunkConfig.luau. Tune spawn rate. Field	Default	EffectDEFAULT_SPAWN_RATE	0.5	Seconds between spawns while the train is running STOPPED_SPAWN_RATE	1.5	Seconds between spawns while the train is braked/stalled Lower values = more frequent spawns. Both JunkService (server) and the spawn scheduler read these. Tune junk movement speed. Field	Default	EffectDEFAULT_JUNK_SPEED	10	Studs per second while train is running STOPPED_JUNK_SPEED	5	Studs per second while train is braked/stalled SPEED_RAMP_DURATION	1.5	Seconds to smoothly transition between speed states SPEED_RAMP_DURATION also controls how smoothly junk decelerates when the train brakes. The first SetTrainState or SetJunkSpeed packet after a client joins snaps to target speed immediately; subsequent ones smoothstep over this duration. Tune despawn distance. JunkConfig.DESPAWN_DISTANCE = 700 -- studs Both the server odometer (JunkService) and client odometer (JunkController) compare accumulated currentSpeed * dt against this value. Increase it to let junk travel farther before disappearing; decrease it to clean up junk sooner. Adjust tier weights.Each tier entry has a Weight field. Selection is weighted-random across tiers. Higher weight = more frequent. Default distribution: Tier 1: 2000 (common) Tier 2: 1000 Tier 3: 10 Tier 4: 5 Tier 5: 0 (currently disabled) To enable Tier 5, set its Weight above 0. To make high-tier junk rarer, reduce Tier 3/4 weights. Adjust type weights and spawn chances within a tier.Inside each tier, Types maps type names (Metal, Wood, Energy) to a rule: Metal = { SpawnChance = 80, Yield = 3 } SpawnChance — probability (0–100) that this type is chosen once its tier is selected.Yield — how many material units are awarded when this junk is collected. To make Energy junk rarer within a tier, lower its SpawnChance relative to Metal/Wood. Tune the pity threshold. JunkConfig.ENERGY_PITY_THRESHOLD = 8 After this many consecutive non-Energy spawns, the next spawn is forced to be Energy. Raise the value to allow longer dry streaks; lower it to guarantee Energy more frequently. Adjust BaseModifiers for live multipliers (if used).BaseModifiers contains runtime-adjustable multipliers that scale spawn rates and per-tier/per-type frequency without rewriting the static tables: BaseModifiers = { GlobalSpawnRateMult = 1.0, TierMultipliers = { [1]=1.0, [2]=1.0, [3]=1.0, [4]=1.0, [5]=1.0 }, TypeMultipliers = { Metal=1.0, Wood=1.0, Energy=1.0 }, } These are applied by JunkService at spawn time. Modifying them at runtime (e.g. from an event/buff system) is safe; they are not cached. Validate spawn volume layout and motion path.After config changes, confirm that spawned junk appears within the intended volume and travels in the direction set by MOVE_DIRECTION (Vector3.new(1, 0, 0) by default). Open the Output window and watch for the JunkConfig: No models found warning — this fires if a JunkAssets tier folder is missing models. Verify the collection loop feels fair.Run a local session, collect junk at the new rate, and confirm the stamina/grabhook gameplay loop still has enough breathing room. If spawn rate is very high, increase MAX_SERVER_JUNKS (200) or MAX_CLIENT_JUNKS (250) to avoid the spawn cap cutting off the flow.

searchDocs.title: Verify in Studio​
searchDocs.content: Run a solo playtest for 2–3 minutes with the Output window open. Confirm the observed spawn frequency roughly matches DEFAULT_SPAWN_RATE, that junk despawns before leaving the visible play area, and that no JunkConfig: warnings appear.    See also: Junk system

searchDocs.title: Steps​
searchDocs.content: Open the stamina/sprint config.Sprint constants share the file src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/StaminaConfig.luau with stamina values. Both SprintController (client) and StaminaManager (server) read from this single config module. Update sprint speed. WalkSpeed = 16 -- base walk speed (studs/s) SprintSpeed = 24 -- speed while sprinting Change SprintSpeed to the desired value. SprintController sets Humanoid.WalkSpeed directly; StaminaManager validates that the client's reported speed is within the expected range. Update FOV. DefaultFOV = 70 -- camera FOV while walking SprintFOV = 85 -- camera FOV while sprinting SprintController animates the transition via MotionMaster. Changing these values alters the start and end points of the FOV tween — no animation code changes are needed. Update keybinds. SprintBinds = { Enum.KeyCode.LeftShift, Enum.KeyCode.ButtonB } Add, remove, or replace entries. Both gamepad and keyboard inputs are accepted in the same array. SprintController reads this array to register UserInputService listeners. If state machine behavior changes, mirror both sides.The sprint lifecycle follows: Idle → Sprinting → Exhausted → Recovering → Idle. If you add a new state transition (e.g. a new "dash" state), you must: Edit src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/SprintController.client.luau for client-side prediction and visual feedback.Edit src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/StaminaManager.luau for server-side authority and packet emission.Update src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/SprintValidation.luau if the validation predicates need to change (e.g. MinMoveDirection, MaxBackwardComponent, MinHorizontalSpeed).Ensure any new packet added is registered in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Packets/init.luau and documented in the networking map. Verify shift-lock interaction.SmoothShiftLock (vendored in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/SmoothShiftLock/) reacts to the sprint state. After changing sprint speed or keybinds, confirm that entering and exiting shift-lock while sprinting does not produce a stuck speed or FOV. Verify placement interaction.Build mode disables sprint while active. After changing sprint config, open build mode, attempt to sprint, and confirm it stays suppressed. Exit build mode and confirm sprint re-enables immediately. Test stamina drain under new speed.If SprintSpeed changed significantly, revisit StaminaDrain and StaminaRegen in the same config to ensure the economy still feels balanced. See Tune Stamina Economy for field details.

searchDocs.title: Verify in Studio​
searchDocs.content: Sprint in a straight line, confirm the WalkSpeed and FOV match the new config values. Trigger shift-lock while sprinting, confirm no stuck state. Enter build mode, confirm sprint is suppressed; exit, confirm sprint resumes. Open the Output window and confirm no StaminaManager sync errors.    See also: Stamina system, Tune Stamina Economy

searchDocs.title: Enable Stash / Move on a Placeable
How it works​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Enable Stash / Move on a Placeable
searchDocs.content: Stash destroys the placed Model and gives the player back the corresponding Tool. Move does the same and then auto-equips the Tool. The action is triggered by ImageButtons in the placeable's existing proximity GUI. The server validates ownership, cooldown, and workspace membership before executing.

searchDocs.title: Checklist​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Enable Stash / Move on a Placeable

searchDocs.title: 1. Confirm the placement Model exists​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Enable Stash / Move on a Placeable
searchDocs.content: ReplicatedStorage/PlaceableItems/<Name> must already exist — this is required for placement itself and is the same model used by Stash/Move.

searchDocs.title: 2. Author the Tool template​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Enable Stash / Move on a Placeable
searchDocs.content: Create (or confirm) a Tool in ReplicatedStorage/PlaceableTools/<Name>.  Create the PlaceableTools folder under ReplicatedStorage if it does not exist yet.Set the attribute PlaceableName = "<Name>" on the Tool root (string attribute, exact match).The Tool must have a Handle BasePart. Author its scripts and behaviour as you would any other placeable tool.  If PlaceableTools/<Name> is missing, both buttons fail silently server-side — no model is destroyed and no item is lost, but the buttons do nothing.

searchDocs.title: 3. Add the buttons to the GUI​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Enable Stash / Move on a Placeable
searchDocs.content: Inside the GUI that the placeable's ProximityPrompt opens, add two ImageButton instances:  One named exactly MoveButtonOne named exactly StashButton  They can be placed at any depth in the GUI's descendant hierarchy. To make them invisible but still clickable, set both ImageTransparency = 1 and BackgroundTransparency = 1 on each button.  If either button is missing, PlaceableActions.bind will log a warning at runtime.

searchDocs.title: 4. Bind and unbind in the controller​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Enable Stash / Move on a Placeable
searchDocs.content: In the controller script that opens and closes the placeable GUI, call PlaceableActions.bind when the GUI opens and binding:Unbind() when it closes:  local PlaceableActions = require(ReplicatedStorage.SharedModules.PlaceableActions) -- When the GUI opens for a specific placed Model: local binding = PlaceableActions.bind(placedModel, guiRoot) -- When the GUI closes (or the controller cleans up): binding:Unbind()   placedModel is the Model instance in workspace.PlacedObjects. guiRoot is the root GUI instance opened by the ProximityPrompt (the ancestor that contains MoveButton and StashButton).  If you use a Janitor for the GUI lifecycle, track the binding with it:  cleaner:Add(binding, "Unbind")

searchDocs.title: 5. (Optional) Configure sound IDs​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Enable Stash / Move on a Placeable
searchDocs.content: File: src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/PlacementConfig.luau (or the equivalent config for your placeable system)  Set PlacementConfig.Sounds.Stash and PlacementConfig.Sounds.Move to the desired rbxassetid:// strings. Leave as "" to disable sound playback for that action.  See Add a Sound if the asset ID does not yet exist in SoundConfig.

searchDocs.title: 6. (Optional) Tune cooldown and poof duration​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Enable Stash / Move on a Placeable
searchDocs.content: In PlacementConfig.PlaceableActions:  Cooldown — minimum seconds between successive Stash/Move requests per player (default 0.4).PoofDuration — how long the shrink-and-disappear visual plays (seconds).

searchDocs.title: Server-side guarantees​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Enable Stash / Move on a Placeable
searchDocs.content: Per-player cooldown gates spam.The target must be a direct child of workspace.PlacedObjects and carry a non-empty PlaceableName attribute (set automatically by PlacementServer at place-time).An atomic claim ensures two players cannot double-grant the same Tool simultaneously.No distance check — the ProximityPrompt enforces proximity at GUI-open time.  On success, every client receives a BroadcastPlaceablePoof packet and renders a transient shrinking clone at the model's position, parented to workspace.PlaceablePoofs and destroyed when the animation completes.

searchDocs.title: Verify in Studio​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Enable Stash / Move on a Placeable
searchDocs.content: Place the item in Studio via the normal placement flow.Walk up to it so the ProximityPrompt activates and the GUI opens.Click StashButton — confirm the model disappears with the poof effect and the Tool appears in your Backpack.Place it again, open the GUI, click MoveButton — confirm the model disappears and the Tool is immediately equipped.Check the Output window for any PlaceableActions warnings about missing buttons or a missing Tool template.    See also: Placeable Actions system reference

searchDocs.title: Change a perk's numeric values​
searchDocs.content: Open src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/PerkConfig.luau and adjust the entry:  PlayerHP = { PerLevel = 0.04, -- ← buff per level (fraction; 0.04 = 4% per level) MaxLevel = 10, -- ← cap ... },   PerLevel is a fraction (not percent). The GUI multiplies by 100 for display. The buff folder attribute is PerLevel * level, so a change here propagates automatically — no code change needed.

searchDocs.title: Add a new perk​
searchDocs.content: Declare it in PerkConfig.Perks.Pick a unique key, a Category ("Personal" or "Party"), a unique BuffKey attribute name, PerLevel, MaxLevel, Order (display order within the tab, no gaps required), DisplayName, and Description (with a %d placeholder for the bonus percent). Wire a consumer.The consumer reads the attribute from the buff folder: Personal: ReplicatedStorage/PerkBuffs/<player.UserId>:GetAttribute(perk.BuffKey)Party: ReplicatedStorage/PartyPerkBuffs:GetAttribute(perk.BuffKey) Read it fresh each time it is needed (or subscribe to GetAttributeChangedSignal if you need live updates). Test in Studio.Join, spend a point, and confirm the attribute value updates in the Explorer. Confirm the consumer responds correctly.

searchDocs.title: Understanding the point economy​
searchDocs.content: Each XP level grants 1 Personal point AND 1 Party point — no separate point storage.Available points = playerLevel - sum(perk levels in that pool).You cannot tune the point grant rate without changing PerkState.available and PerkManager.replicate in tandem. There is intentionally no config for it.

searchDocs.title: Respec (no cost)​
searchDocs.content: Players can respec either pool freely from the GUI. The server clears the relevant entries in PerkLevels; available points return to the wallet automatically.

searchDocs.title: Verify in Studio​
searchDocs.content: Join in Studio with API Services enabled.Open the perk panel (bottom-center "Perks" button).Spend a point on a perk and confirm: The level counter increments.In Explorer, ReplicatedStorage/PerkBuffs/<UserId> shows the updated attribute.The downstream consumer reflects the change (e.g. Humanoid MaxHealth for Vitality). Respec and confirm levels reset and points return.    See also: Perks system

searchDocs.title: Steps​
searchDocs.content: Open the shredder config.All shredder constants live in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/ShredderConfig.luau. Tune hold duration.The required hold scales linearly between one junk item and MAX_JUNK_COUNT items: Field	Default	EffectMIN_HOLD_DURATION	0.3 s	Hold time required for exactly 1 junk item MAX_HOLD_DURATION	3.5 s	Hold time required when carrying MAX_JUNK_COUNT or more items MAX_JUNK_COUNT	10	Junk count at which duration is fully capped at MAX_HOLD_DURATION Increase MAX_HOLD_DURATION to make large batches feel weightier. Keep MIN_HOLD_DURATION above the sum of normal round-trip latency to avoid the server rejecting fast single-item shreds. Tune arc animation. Field	Default	EffectARC_HEIGHT_BOOST	5 studs	Extra Y added to the bezier midpoint — controls arc peak height ARC_DURATION	0.55 s	Travel time per material Tool from spawn to landing ITEM_EJECT_DELAY	0.125 s	Stagger between consecutive ejected materials LANDING_SCATTER_RADIUS	1.5 studs	Random spread around LandingPoint for a natural pile effect MAX_ANIMATED_EJECT_ITEMS	60	Cap on visually animated items per shred MAX_STREAM_DURATION	6.0 s	Budget cap for the full ejection stream (compresses delay if needed) Handle anti-exploit tolerances with care.These fields directly affect server-side rejection rates. Tighten them only after validating against real network conditions: Field	Default	Risk of over-tighteningINTERACT_DISTANCE_TOLERANCE	5 studs	Added on top of INTERACT_DISTANCE (10 studs) server-side to cover positional desync. Reducing below 3 will cause false rejections on high-latency clients. HOLD_COMPLETION_TOLERANCE	0.5 s	Subtracted from required hold when server validates timing. Setting below 0.3 will reject legitimate completions on 150ms+ RTT connections. PER_PLAYER_COOLDOWN	1.0 s	Minimum gap between consecutive successful shreds per player. Do not set below 0.5 s. Adjust material yield.Material types produced by a shred are determined by JunkConfig.MaterialRules in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/JunkConfig.luau: MaterialRules = { Metal = {"Metal"}, Wood = {"Wood"}, Energy = {"Energy"}, } To add a new material output type, add an entry here and create a matching Tool template inside the CraftingMaterials folder in ReplicatedStorage (see step 6). After changing these mappings, re-test ShredderServer.buildMaterialSequence output in Studio. Verify Studio asset setup before testing.The shredder system requires the following to be in place in the live place: Each workbench Model in Workspace must be tagged Workbench (CollectionService).Each workbench Model must have its PrimaryPart set.Each workbench must contain a child Model named TrajectoryPoints (field: TRAJECTORY_MODEL_NAME) with two invisible, anchored, non-collidable BasePart children: SpawnPoint (field: SPAWN_POINT_NAME) and LandingPoint (field: LANDING_POINT_NAME). Tag this model with PlacementIgnore.ReplicatedStorage must contain a Folder named CraftingMaterials (field: MATERIALS_FOLDER) with Tool templates: Wood, Metal (and any new types). Each Tool must have a BasePart child named Handle and CanBeDropped = false.Missing templates cause ShredderServer.ejectMaterials to fail silently. Test auto-collect delay.After ejection, materials lying on the floor auto-move to the owner's Backpack after: AUTO_COLLECT_DELAY = 45 -- seconds Adjust this if the window feels too long or too short for your gameplay loop.

searchDocs.title: Verify in Studio​
searchDocs.content: Run a solo session, carry a mix of junk counts (1 item, 5 items, 10 items), and hold the shredder interaction. Confirm hold durations roughly match the linear interpolation between MIN_HOLD_DURATION and MAX_HOLD_DURATION. Watch the arc animation and confirm materials land near LandingPoint. Check the Output window — a missing CraftingMaterials template will print a warning but not throw a visible error.    See also: Shredder system, Adjust Junk Flow

searchDocs.title: Steps​
searchDocs.content: Open the stamina config.All tunable constants live in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/StaminaConfig.luau. This file is shared between client and server, so one edit propagates to both sides. Adjust core stamina values. Field	Default	EffectMaxStamina	100	Pool ceiling StaminaDrain	10	Units drained per second while sprinting StaminaRegen	15	Units regenerated per second when not sprinting RegenDelay	1.4	Seconds after sprint ends before regen starts Adjust sprint feel. Field	Default	EffectWalkSpeed	16	Base walk speed (studs/s) SprintSpeed	24	Speed while sprinting DefaultFOV	70	Camera FOV at walk SprintFOV	85	Camera FOV during sprint FOV transitions are animated by SprintController; changing the values here is enough — no animation code changes needed. Adjust sprint keybinds (if needed).The SprintBinds array accepts any mix of Enum.KeyCode and Enum.UserInputType values: SprintBinds = { Enum.KeyCode.LeftShift, Enum.KeyCode.ButtonB }, Add or replace entries. Both SprintController and StaminaManager read from the same config array. Tune buff parameters.Three buff types are defined; each has a Duration (seconds) and, where applicable, a Strength multiplier: StaminaRegenBuff = { Strength = 1.75, Duration = 18 } -- multiplies StaminaRegen StaminaUsageBuff = { Strength = 0.5, Duration = 15 } -- multiplies StaminaDrain InfiniteStaminaBuff = { Duration = 10 } -- disables drain entirely Strength is a multiplier applied to the base drain or regen rate. A Strength below 1.0 on StaminaUsageBuff means less drain (easier). Update buff icons (if adding a new icon).Icon asset IDs are in BuffIcons: BuffIcons = { InfiniteStamina = "rbxassetid://136295729783969", RegenMultiplier = "rbxassetid://126110497899525", UsageMultiplier = "rbxassetid://116908939168654", } Replace the rbxassetid://... string with a new uploaded asset ID. Validate client feel and server authority.SprintController (client) predicts drain and regen locally. StaminaManager (server) is the source of truth and corrects the client via packets. After saving, test in a live Studio session: sprint until exhausted, confirm drain/regen rates match the new values, and confirm the server correction does not cause jarring snaps. Test buff interactions.Trigger each buff type (via a test script or the existing pickup pathway) while sprinting. Confirm: StaminaRegenBuff accelerates refill during and after sprint.StaminaUsageBuff visibly slows drain while active.InfiniteStaminaBuff allows indefinite sprinting with no drain.

searchDocs.title: Verify in Studio​
searchDocs.content: Sprint until stamina is depleted, release sprint, and confirm the regen delay then regen rate match the new config values. Trigger a buff and confirm it overrides base rates correctly. Check the Output window for any StaminaManager sync errors.    See also: Stamina system

searchDocs.title: Steps​
searchDocs.content: Open the placement config.Visual and icon settings live in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/PlacementConfig.luau. Replace icon asset IDs.The Icons table holds one entry per toolbar button: Icons = { GridOn = "rbxassetid://118749020984103", GridOff = "rbxassetid://132920215751528", GhostUnlocked = "rbxassetid://132512888685903", GhostLocked = "rbxassetid://128344634676430", } Replace the rbxassetid://... value for any icon you want to update. Upload the new image in Studio's Asset Manager first to get a valid asset ID. The key names (GridOn, GridOff, GhostUnlocked, GhostLocked) must remain unchanged — BuildModeGuiController looks them up by key. Adjust ghost appearance. Field	Default	EffectVisualGhostTransparency	0.45	Opacity of main model parts during ghost preview CollisionBoxGhostTransparency	0.65	Opacity of the CollisionBox part during preview OtherGhostVisualTransparency	0.60	Opacity of other parts in other players' ghosts ShowCollisionBox	false	Set true to make CollisionBox visible during preview (debug aid) ColorValid	Color3.fromRGB(100, 210, 255)	Tint when placement is valid ColorInvalid	Color3.fromRGB(255, 80, 80)	Tint when placement is blocked ColorTweenTime	0.12 s	Duration of color transition between valid/invalid states Adjust ghost movement responsiveness. Field	Default	EffectFreeModeLerpSpeed	20	How quickly the ghost follows the cursor in free mode RotationLerpSpeed	15	How quickly the ghost rotates when the player rotates the item GhostUpdateHz	20	Raycast update rate (Hz) — lower values reduce CPU cost but feel less smooth Adjust the grid overlay. Field	Default	EffectGridTextureId	"rbxassetid://6372755229"	Decal texture applied to build area surfaces during grid mode GridTransparency	0.35	Opacity of the grid overlay (0 = opaque, 1 = invisible) Keep the button-to-signal mapping consistent.src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/BuildModeGuiController.client.luau wires each toolbar button to a Signals event. If you add a new button (e.g. a new toggle), you must: Add the new icon key to PlacementConfig.Icons.Create a corresponding Signals entry in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Signals/init.luau if the button drives new behavior.Wire the button in BuildModeGuiController to fire/subscribe to that signal.Update the signals map (and the networking map if the signal crosses the client/server boundary). Do not add raw RemoteEvent calls from BuildModeGuiController — all cross-boundary communication must go through Packets. Test mobile input parity.Build mode must be fully operable without a keyboard. In a Studio mobile emulation session (or on device): Confirm all toolbar buttons are reachable and tap targets are large enough.Confirm grid/free toggle and rotation controls work via touch.Confirm the ghost follows touch drag correctly. Test desktop input parity.In a standard Studio session: Confirm keyboard shortcuts for grid toggle and rotation still fire correctly after any icon or signal changes.Confirm the cursor-following ghost is smooth at the configured GhostUpdateHz.

searchDocs.title: Verify in Studio​
searchDocs.content: Open build mode on both a desktop and a mobile-emulated client. Toggle grid on/off and confirm the correct GridOn/GridOff icon appears. Hover over a valid and an invalid surface and confirm the ghost color transitions. Check the Output window for any missing-asset warnings from BuildModeGuiController.    See also: Placement system, Add a New Placeable Item

searchDocs.title: Runtime buff folders​
searchDocs.content: These are not config modules but runtime ReplicatedStorage folders written by dispatchers and read by gameplay systems. Listed here because their writer/reader contracts are as important to maintain as static config.  Folder / Attribute	Writer	Reader(s)	NotesReplicatedStorage/TechTreeBuffs.FuelEfficiency	TechEffectsDispatcher (applyFuelEfficiency)	TrainFuelManager	Drain multiplier written as current * (1 / Multiplier); defaults to 1.0 (no effect) until Fuel_T1 unlocks. Stacks multiplicatively with PartyPerkBuffs.FuelEfficiencyBonus — see Tech Tree. ReplicatedStorage/TechTreeBuffs.MaxHP	TechEffectsDispatcher (applyStatBuff)	TrainShieldManager.recomputeMax	Numeric accumulation; each Durability node unlock adds Effect.Amount (Durability_T1 +50, Durability_T2 +150). Read as additive shield capacity: maxShield = (BASE_SHIELD + MaxHP) * (1 + TrainShieldBonus). ReplicatedStorage/PerkBuffs/<UserId>.DamageBonus	PerkEffectsDispatcher	WeaponServer (scaledDamage helper, all 5 player-attack sites, applied after headshot multiplier)	Personal perk; read server-side via FindFirstChild(tostring(player.UserId)). ReplicatedStorage/PerkBuffs/<UserId>.CoinGainBonus	PerkEffectsDispatcher	CoinManager.AddCoins	Personal perk; applied as math.max(1, math.floor(amount * (1 + bonus))) — 1-coin floor. ReplicatedStorage/PartyPerkBuffs.FuelEfficiencyBonus	PerkEffectsDispatcher	TrainFuelManager	Party perk (server-max resolution); combined with TechTreeBuffs.FuelEfficiency multiplicatively: effectiveRate = baseRate × max(0.1, TechTreeBuffs.FuelEfficiency × max(0.1, 1 − FuelEfficiencyBonus)). ReplicatedStorage/PartyPerkBuffs.TrainShieldBonus	PerkEffectsDispatcher	TrainShieldManager.recomputeMax	Party perk (server-max resolution); 0.05 * maxLevel. Combined with TechTreeBuffs.MaxHP multiplicatively: maxShield = (BASE_SHIELD + MaxHP) * (1 + TrainShieldBonus). ReplicatedStorage/ArmorState/<UserId>.ArmorBaseReduction	ArmorManager	HealthManager (applyDamageInternal)	Per-player crafted-armor base reduction (fraction); combined with PerkBuffs/<UserId>.ArmorEfficiency at the damage sink: clamp(ArmorBaseReduction * (1 + ArmorEfficiency), 0, ArmorConfig.MaxReductionCap). Defaults to 0 (tier 0 / unarmored).

searchDocs.title: Notes​
searchDocs.content: We do not re-document third-party libraries. Only heavily-modified in-tree dependencies (Packets, MotionMaster, Signals) have their own documentation pages.The TweenPlus TweenPreallocations attribute must be re-set in Studio after everywally install. Details are on the Toolchain page.Janitor usage patterns — one Janitor per scope, Cleanup vs Destroy, keyed collections — are covered on Janitor Patterns.

searchDocs.title: Requirements​
searchDocs.content: The caller supplies a GuiButton that already contains:  an Option child (TextLabel) — shows the current selection's label,an Arrow child (ImageLabel) — flips up/down as the list opens/closes.  The widget builds the option list beneath the button at runtime.

searchDocs.title: API​
searchDocs.content: local Dropdown = require(SharedModules.Gui.Dropdown) type Option = { Value: string, Label: string } type Config = { StartValue: string?, -- initial selection (no .Changed fired) OptionTemplate: GuiButton?, -- cloned per row; needs a "Label" TextLabel. Else rows are styled from the button. MaxVisible: number?, -- cap visible rows; scroll beyond RowHeight: number?, -- pixel height per row (default 28) ArrowUp: string?, ArrowDown: string?, -- arrow image overrides } local dropdown = Dropdown.new(button, options, config?)   Instance members:  .Changed: Signal<string> — fires the selected Value when the selection changes.:Select(value) — select by Value programmatically.:GetValue(): string? — current Value.:Show(visible) — open/close the list.:Destroy() — disconnect everything and remove the built list frame.

searchDocs.title: Notes​
searchDocs.content: The host ScreenGui should use Global ZIndexBehavior so the open list (high ZIndex) draws over sibling content.All connections are owned by a Janitor and released on :Destroy().When no OptionTemplate is given, each row's Label is a clone of the button's Option label, so rows inherit its text styling (alignment,TextScaled, font, RichText, child UIPadding) and stay in sync if the button is restyled. Because TextScaled is inherited, row text scales toRowHeight; set RowHeight to the button's pixel height to match its text size exactly.

searchDocs.title: Core rule: one Janitor per lifecycle scope​
searchDocs.content: Each distinct lifecycle gets exactly one Janitor. When that lifecycle ends, call:Cleanup or :Destroy on it (see below for which to use).  local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local Janitor = require(ReplicatedStorage.Packages.Janitor) local janitor = Janitor.new() -- Track a signal connection (cleaned up by calling :Disconnect) janitor:Add(inst.Event:Connect(fn), "Disconnect") -- Track an Instance (cleaned up by calling :Destroy) janitor:Add(part, "Destroy") -- Tear down and reuse (leaves the Janitor alive for the next cycle) janitor:Cleanup() -- Tear down and discard (the Janitor itself is gone afterward) janitor:Destroy()

searchDocs.title: Cleanup vs Destroy​
searchDocs.content: Method	When to use	Typical example:Cleanup()	The Janitor is module-level and reused across respawns or re-equips.	characterJanitor, backpackJanitor — cleaned on every CharacterAdded, then refilled. :Destroy()	The Janitor is created per-entry and discarded when the entry is removed.	WorkbenchEntry.Cleaner, engine/lever entry janitors.  Using :Destroy on a reused janitor silently breaks the next cycle because the object becomes unusable. Using :Cleanup on a per-entry janitor leaks the janitor table itself. Match the method to the ownership model.

searchDocs.title: Keyed-collection pattern​
searchDocs.content: When managing a dynamic set of entries (workbenches, junk pickups, registered engines, etc.), give each entry its own Janitor stored under a predictable key:  -- Type annotation (Luau) type Entry = { model: Model, cleaner: Janitor.Janitor, } local registry: { [string]: Entry } = {} local function register(id: string, model: Model) local entry: Entry = { model = model, cleaner = Janitor.new(), } entry.cleaner:Add(model, "Destroy") entry.cleaner:Add(model.ChildAdded:Connect(function(child) -- ... end), "Disconnect") registry[id] = entry end local function unregister(id: string) local entry = registry[id] if entry then entry.cleaner:Destroy() -- per-entry → Destroy registry[id] = nil end end   The pattern guarantees that removing an entry also disconnects every signal and destroys every instance that entry owns, with no possibility of leaking a handle.

searchDocs.title: Singleton exception​
searchDocs.content: Top-level controller connections that live for the full session do not need a Janitor. If the connection is created once at script root and never torn down (for example, Players.LocalPlayer.CharacterAdded at the top of a client controller), wrapping it in a Janitor adds overhead with no benefit.  Only use a Janitor when the scope can end before the script does.

searchDocs.title: Quick TweenService equivalence​
searchDocs.content: -- TweenService (do NOT use this in client code) TweenService:Create(target, TweenInfo.new(0.5, Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.Out), goals):Play() -- MotionMaster equivalent MotionMaster.Play(target, goals, { Duration = 0.5, Model = "EaseOutQuad" })

searchDocs.title: MotionMaster.Play(target, goals, config)​
searchDocs.content: Fire-and-forget shorthand. Creates a TweenObject, calls :Play(), and returns it.  MotionMaster.Play(frame, { BackgroundTransparency = 0 }, { Duration = 0.3, Model = "EaseOutQuad" })

searchDocs.title: MotionMaster.Create(target, goals, config)​
searchDocs.content: Returns a TweenObject for manual lifecycle control. Does not start playback.  local tween = MotionMaster.Create(label, { TextTransparency = 1 }, { Duration = 0.5 }) tween:Play()   TweenObject methods​  Method	Description:Play()	Start or restart from current elapsed position. :Pause()	Pause; preserves elapsed time. :Resume()	Resume a paused tween. :Cancel()	Pause and reset to the start value. :Reverse()	Flip direction mid-playback; elapsed time mirrors continuously. :Scrub(alpha)	Jump to a normalized position [0, 1] without playback. :Destroy()	Disconnect all connections and release memory. :OnStep(cb)	Register cb(alpha, dt) — fires every frame. Chainable. :OnComplete(cb)	Register cb() — fires when the tween finishes. Chainable. :OnDestroy(cb)	Register cb() — fires on :Destroy(). Chainable.

searchDocs.title: MotionMaster.Spring(target, prop, config)​
searchDocs.content: Creates and starts a SpringDriver that follows a dynamically updated endpoint. Supports number and Vector3 properties only.  local driver = MotionMaster.Spring(frame, "Position", { Omega = 18, Zeta = 1.0 }) driver:SetTarget(newPosition) -- update the goal at any time   SpringDriver config fields: Omega (natural frequency), Zeta (damping ratio),MaxSubsteps, FixedDt.  SpringDriver methods: :SetTarget(v), :OnStep(cb), :IsSettled(eps?), :Stop(), :Destroy().

searchDocs.title: MotionMaster.fromPreset(presetName, target, prop)​
searchDocs.content: Instantiate a SpringDriver from one of the 16 named presets.  local driver = MotionMaster.fromPreset("UIPanel", frame, "Position")   Named spring presets​  Category	PresetsUI / Interface	UIPanel, UIFade, UIBounce, UISnap Camera	CameraFollow, CameraLag, CameraShake Gameplay objects	RecoilCritical, RecoilSnappy, DoorBouncy, DoorStiff, WeaponSway, JiggleBone Environment	HoverStabilizer, SpringPlatform, HeavyGate

searchDocs.title: MotionMaster.Sequence(config)​
searchDocs.content: Chain or parallelize TweenObjects. Returns a Sequence.  local seq = MotionMaster.Sequence() -- serial (default) seq:Add(tweenA) seq:Add(tweenB, 0.1) -- 0.1 s gap before tweenB seq:Play() local par = MotionMaster.Sequence({ Parallel = true }) -- all at once par:Add(tweenC) par:Add(tweenD) par:OnComplete(function() print("all done") end) par:Play()   Sequence methods: :Add(tweenObj, delay?), :Play(), :OnComplete(cb), :Destroy().

searchDocs.title: MotionMaster.SplineMove(target, controlPoints, config)​
searchDocs.content: Moves target (a BasePart) along an arc-length-reparameterized Catmull-Rom spline.controlPoints is an array of BasePart instances or Vector3 values (minimum 2).  local tween = MotionMaster.SplineMove(cart, { p0, p1, p2, p3 }, { Duration = 4, Model = "EaseInOutCubic", ConstantSpeed = true, -- default true for SplineMove }) tween:Play()   Returns a TweenObject (same lifecycle methods as above).

searchDocs.title: MotionMaster.PivotMove(model, targetCFrame, config)​
searchDocs.content: Animates a Model via :PivotTo(), preserving relative part offsets. Accepts a CFrame as the goal.  local tween = MotionMaster.PivotMove(door, openCFrame, { Duration = 0.8, Model = "DoorBouncy", -- preset name accepted for Model field }) tween:Play()

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: External signal fires Signals.RequestShootingCamera(true/false) └─> CameraController sets aimMode, calls applyState() ├─ offsetSpring:SetTarget(ShootingOffset or ThirdPersonOffset) ├─ humanoid.AutoRotate = false (aim) / false (locked 3P) / true (free) ├─ MouseBehavior = LockCenter (aim/locked-no-cursor) or Default (free-look OR GUI cursor request) ├─ reticleImage.Visible = aimMode └─> Signals.OnShootingCameraToggled:Fire(aimMode) └─> CameraBoomController switches max-zoom ceiling LeftAlt key pressed (non-aim only) └─> freeLookMode toggles -> applyState() RunService RenderStep "CameraUpdate" (Priority = Camera + 1) ├─ aim : lerp HRP.CFrame to face camera yaw └─> locked 3P: lerp HRP.CFrame to face movement direction RunService RenderStep "CameraBoom" (Priority = Camera) ├─ raycast from camera.Focus toward camera.CFrame.Position ├─ clamp hit distance by BoomBuffer └─> player.CameraMaxZoomDistance = smoothed clamped distance

searchDocs.title: Client / Server / Shared​
searchDocs.content: The camera system is client-only — there is no server component.  CameraController.client.luau  Owns the two state booleans:  aimMode — set exclusively via Signals.RequestShootingCamera. No player keybind activates aim directly; only tools (GrabHook on equip), weapons (WeaponController on weapon equip/unequip), and systems (PlacementClient on build-mode entry) fire this signal.freeLookMode — toggled by LeftAlt; inert while aimMode is true. Aim always wins: when aimMode is true, LeftAlt presses are silently consumed.  On every character load a new MotionMaster.Spring is created bound to humanoid.CameraOffset (destroyed on CharacterRemoving). The spring's Omega and Zeta come from CameraConfig. The render step runs at Camera + 1 priority so it executes after CameraBoom.  CameraBoomController.client.luau  Raycasts from camera.Focus toward camera.CFrame.Position every frame, excluding the local character. If the ray hits geometry, player.CameraMaxZoomDistance is set to hitDistance - BoomBuffer, clamped to [CameraMinZoomDistance, maxForMode]. The result is lerp-smoothed by BoomSmoothingSpeed * dt. The ceiling for maxForMode switches between ShootingCameraMaxZoomDistance (aim) and ThirdPersonCameraMaxZoomDistance (third-person) when Signals.OnShootingCameraToggled fires.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Aim mode is signal-only There is no keybind that activates aimMode directly. Only external systems fire Signals.RequestShootingCamera. If a new tool or system needs to enter aim mode it must fire this signal — do not read or write the aimMode local directly.  Do not use TweenService to animate CameraOffset. The offset spring is a MotionMaster.Spring driver; bypassing it will produce conflicting states and the spring will override any TweenService tween on the next frame.The CameraBoom render step runs at Camera priority, one tick before CameraUpdate at Camera + 1. Do not change these priorities — ordering matters for the zoom clamp to see the correct camera position before HRP rotation is applied.The offset spring is re-created on every CharacterAdded and destroyed on CharacterRemoving. Holding a reference to an old spring past the character death will produce a dangling driver pointing at a destroyed Humanoid.freeLookMode re-enables humanoid.AutoRotate and unlocks the mouse. Any system that expects AutoRotate = false (e.g. shift-lock integrations) should listen to OnShootingCameraToggled rather than polling AutoRotate.A GUI that needs a clickable cursor fires Signals.RequestMouseIcon:Fire(true); while set (and not aiming) the camera holds MouseBehavior = Default and shows the cursor, restoring LockCenter on Fire(false). The PC gate lives in the producer (WorkbenchGuiController), so the camera frees the mouse whenever asked regardless of platform.

searchDocs.title: Placement → mount → fire​
searchDocs.content: Place — the cannon is a placeable (PlaceableItems/Cannon + PlaceableTools/Cannon). Placement, stash, and move are inherited from the placement system; the placed clone lands in workspace/PlacedObjects with a PlaceableName = "Cannon" attribute.Mount — CannonController attaches a ProximityPrompt to each placed cannon'sMountPromptPart. Triggering it sends ReqMountCannon(model); the server validates proximity + single-occupancy and records the gunner. Mounting locks the gunner's movement and shows a ballistic arc preview.Fire — input sends ReqFireCannon(muzzle, aimDir). The server validates occupancy, cooldown, and overheat, then simulates the shell from its own muzzle CFrame with a gravity Acceleration. On impact it applies Damage × (1 + CannonDamageBonus) viaCombatService.ApplyAOE and broadcasts CannonFired (muzzle flash + barrel snap + sound) and ExplosionAt (boom).

searchDocs.title: Overheat​
searchDocs.content: Each shot adds HeatPerShot; heat decays at HeatDecayPerSec. Reaching MaxHeat locks the cannon for OverheatLockTime. Heat (0–1) and Overheated are attributes on the placed Model (no packet); CannonGuiController reads them to drive the gunner's heat bar.

searchDocs.title: Server authority & anti-exploit​
searchDocs.content: Occupancy, cooldown, overheat-lock, and shell origin are all re-validated server-side; the server fires from its own muzzle, so a forged origin/aim cannot help. Single occupant per cannon (a live occupant blocks takeover; a dead one is replaced). CannonDamageBonusis read server-side from the server-written PartyPerkBuffs folder per shot — unforgeable. Faction routing is inherited from CombatService, so EnemyNPC rigs must be in a hostile faction to take player damage.

searchDocs.title: EnemyShip forward seam​
searchDocs.content: CannonServer.applyCannonAOE damages Humanoids via CombatService and decrements a numeric Health attribute on in-radius models tagged EnemyShip (linear falloff, destroy at ≤0). This is inert until the future enemy-ship spec tags ships; it requires no change to the perk hook.

searchDocs.content: Config: ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/CannonConfig.luauServer: ServerScriptService/CannonServer.server.luauClient: StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/CannonController.client.luau,CannonGuiController.client.luauPackets: ReqMountCannon, ReqFireCannon, CannonFired (impact reuses ExplosionAt)Signal: OnCannonMounted

searchDocs.title: API​
searchDocs.content: Function	DescriptionDamageNumbers.Show(worldPosition, amount, styleName?)	Spawn a number. No-op if disabled or amount <= 0. styleName defaults to the config default; unknown names fall back to it. DamageNumbers.SetEnabled(value)	Toggle spawning of new numbers (for a settings menu). In-flight numbers finish. DamageNumbers.IsEnabled()	Returns the current toggle state. DamageNumbers.Init()	Build + pre-warm the pool. Idempotent; lazy-runs on first Show otherwise. Called once by DamageNumbersController.

searchDocs.title: Behaviour​
searchDocs.content: Each number is a pooled BillboardGui (GenericPoolInstance). On Show it acquires an entry, applies a named style (color/font/size/stroke), offsets the spawn by a random jitter so rapid hits fan out, then animates withMotionMaster:  Pop — UIScale.Scale from Pop.StartScale to 1 with a back-out overshoot.Rise — BillboardGui.StudsOffsetWorldSpace.Y drifts up by Rise.Heightover the lifetime.Fade — text/stroke transparency goes to 1 during the finalFade.Duration.  When the rise finishes, the entry's Janitor is destroyed and the part returns to the pool. The billboard uses world-space (Scale) sizing, so numbers shrink with camera distance and cull past Billboard.MaxDistance.

searchDocs.title: Tuning​
searchDocs.content: All tuning is inConfigs/DamageNumberConfig: Styles (named presets — normal, crit,heal out of the box), Pop/Rise/Fade/Lifetime timing, Jitter, Poolsizing, and Billboard size/distance. Add a new look by adding a Stylesentry and passing its name to Show.

searchDocs.title: Out of scope​
searchDocs.content: No combat wiring, Packets, or Signals — a damage source (client predicted or a server damage broadcast) calls Show directly. The settings menu just calls SetEnabled. The toggle is not persisted.

searchDocs.title: Data model​
searchDocs.content: The PlayerCoins profile stores a single value, Coins. STORE_NAME("PlayerCoins") and the UserId key are identical in every place of the universe, so the lobby and gameplay share one DataStore record; ProfileStore session-locking serializes the teleport handoff. All bounds live inConfigs/CoinConfig.luau (STARTING_BALANCE, MAX_BALANCE).

searchDocs.title: API (server-authoritative)​
searchDocs.content: CoinManager (ServerStorage) is the sole authority:  CoinManager.GetCoins(player): number — current balance, 0 if no profile.CoinManager.AddCoins(player, amount, reason?) — award coins; no-op ifamount <= 0 or no profile; clamps to MAX_BALANCE. reason is an optional source tag logged server-side.CoinManager.DeductCoins(player, amount): boolean — atomic spend; returnsfalse with no mutation on amount <= 0, missing profile, or insufficient funds.CoinManager.Initialize() — wires the profile lifecycle; called once byCoinSystemLoader in both places.

searchDocs.title: Replication​
searchDocs.content: Every successful mutation fires CoinStateSync (balance: U32) to the owning client. CoinController re-fires it as Signals.OnCoinsChanged(balance) for a future coin HUD. There is no client→server packet — earning and spending are fully server-driven.

searchDocs.title: Out of scope (future work)​
searchDocs.content: Earning sources (gameplay-session completion, daily/weekly challenges), sinks (shop + purchase packet), and the coin HUD are separate systems that call theCoinManager API; they are not part of the wallet module.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: Player equips GrabHook tool • mouse.TargetFilter = PlacedObjects folder (so placed items don't occlude aim) • Signals.RequestShootingCamera:Fire(true) ──► CameraController enters aim mode RenderStepped (every frame while equipped) • GetAimedJunk(): Spherecast from handle attachment toward mouse.Hit - radius = Physics.HitboxRadius (2 studs) - max distance = Physics.MaxDistance (150 studs) - angle gate: must be within 90° of character forward vector • if junk found → ShowForceField(junkPart, junkId) [highlight effect] • if aim lost for > 0.08 s grace → HideForceField Player clicks (tool.Activated) • cooldown check (Physics.Cooldown = 1.1 s) • Signals.TryClaimJunk:Fire(id, hitPoint) ──────────────────────────► JunkController → Packets.ReqJunkClaim → JunkService (server) ← BeginJunkRetract (broadcast) • FireGrappleAndAttach(targetPart, hitPoint, junkId, token): 1. Instance.new("Attachment") on junk part ("HookAttachment") 2. GrabHookVisuals.CreateBeam(handleAtt, junkAtt, targetPart) 3. GrabHookVisuals.AnimateProjectile → three-phase animation: FLIGHT: junkAtt.WorldPosition lerps toward junk at Physics.Speed (200 studs/s) beam curves oscillate (Amplitude=12, Frequency=40, Decay=4) LATCH: single transition frame, curves flattened to 0 RETRACT: targetPart.Position lerps back to handle at Physics.RetractSpeed (50 studs/s) 4. on retract complete → Signals.TryFinalizeJunk:Fire(id) ─────────► JunkController → Packets.ReqJunkFinalize → JunkService ← JunkCollected (broadcast) • SoundManager.PlaySFXAt("GrabHookFire") — replicated to all clients • SoundManager.PlayLooped("GrabHookLoop") with fade-in/out scheduling Player unequips tool • fireToken incremented (invalidates all pending task.delay callbacks) • loopHandle:Destroy() • Signals.RequestShootingCamera:Fire(false) ──► CameraController exits aim mode

searchDocs.title: Client / Server / Shared​
searchDocs.content: Client (GrabHook.client.luau)  Runs entirely as a LocalScript inside the Grabhook Tool under StarterPack.GetAimedJunk(rootPart) performs a Spherecast from the handle's Attachment.WorldPosition toward mouse.Hit.Position. Junk ID is resolved by invoking GetJunkIdFromPart via BindableCore (registered by JunkController).A force-field highlight (ReplicatedStorage/ForceField template cloned to workspace) tracks the currently aimed junk part on every RenderStepped tick. A 0.08-second grace window prevents flickering when the spherecast briefly misses.On activation: fires Signals.TryClaimJunk (JunkController handles the network call), increments fireToken to version all pending callbacks, then calls FireGrappleAndAttach.FireGrappleAndAttach creates an Attachment on the target junk part, creates a Beam via GrabHookVisuals.CreateBeam, and calls GrabHookVisuals.AnimateProjectile. When retraction completes, it fires Signals.TryFinalizeJunk and plays a positional pickup sound at the character's CollisionPart/UpperTorso/HumanoidRootPart anchor resolved by CharacterAnchor.Loop sound (GrabHookLoop) is scheduled with a LoopStartDelay (0.15 s) fade-in and timed fade-out matched to the total hook animation duration.  Server (JunkService.server.luau)  Validates ReqJunkClaim: reconstructs junk world position from SpawnPos + MOVE_DIRECTION * (junkOdometer - SpawnOdometer), checks player distance against GrabHookConfig.Physics.MaxDistance + 15 studs, enforces per-player cooldown, and reserves the junk.Validates ReqJunkFinalize: checks reservation ownership and the 5-second timeout, marks the junk collected, broadcasts JunkCollected, and gives the corresponding tool to player.Backpack.See Junk for the full server-side claim/finalize detail.  Shared (GrabHookVisuals.luau)  CreateBeam(att0, att1, parent) — instantiates a Beam and copies all properties from GrabHookConfig.Visuals onto it.AnimateProjectile(beam, startAtt, targetPart, hitPos, onCleanup) — three-phase RenderStepped loop (Flight / Latch / Retract). Aborts if targetPart leaves workspace (e.g. pool reclaim). Calls onCleanup when retraction completes or on abort.AnimateObserver(beam, startAtt) — simpler decay loop for other players watching the retraction animation, started by JunkController on BeginJunkRetract.
