searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Server proximity check uses a latency slack of 15 studs The claim check compares the player's position against the reconstructed junk position with GrabHookConfig.Physics.MaxDistance + 15. The extra 15 studs compensates for network latency. Increasing MaxDistance without adjusting the slack (or vice versa) can allow or block claims unexpectedly.  Shift-lock / aim camera interplay. Equipping the GrabHook fires Signals.RequestShootingCamera(true) to enter aim mode. Unequipping fires (false) to exit. If you add another system that also drives RequestShootingCamera, ensure the signals do not conflict (last writer wins).mouse.TargetFilter = PlacedObjects prevents placed items from blocking the aim raycast. If new workspace folders are added for collidable world geometry that should also be ignored, add them to the filter.fireToken versioning. Incrementing fireToken on unequip cancels all pending task.delay callbacks (sound fade-out, finalize). Never skip the token check inside scheduled callbacks or sounds will play on the next hook cycle.Force-field template must exist. GrabHook.client uses ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("ForceField") at startup. If the template is missing, the script will yield indefinitely.Beam and attachment cleanup. AnimateProjectile destroys both the Beam and the HookAttachment on cleanup. If you add more attachments or constraints to the junk part during a hook cycle, extend the CleanupJunkModel function in JunkController to remove them on pool return.CharacterAnchor resolves the positional SFX anchor. The pickup sound plays at CollisionPart → UpperTorso → HumanoidRootPart (first found). SingleCollider avatars that lack HumanoidRootPart but have CollisionPart are handled correctly.

searchDocs.title: EnemySpawnGroup​
searchDocs.content: A spawn group is a Model in the DataModel tagged with the CollectionService tag EnemySpawnGroup. The group's identity is its GroupName string attribute; if the attribute is absent the model's .Name is used. The tag is all that is required — any Model (a pirate ship, an outpost building, a plain Part wrapped in a Model) becomes a valid group.  Because spawn-point attachments are descendants of the group Model, their .WorldPosition moves automatically with the model's CFrame. Placing the group on a moving ship and then calling SpawnWave will place enemies relative to the ship's current pose at spawn time, with no code changes.

searchDocs.title: EnemySpawnPoint​
searchDocs.content: Each spawn point is an Attachment tagged EnemySpawnPoint, parented anywhere beneath the group model. Two optional per-point attributes control selection and jitter:  Attribute	Type	Default	PurposeRadius	number	archetype DefaultRadius → DEFAULT_POINT_RADIUS	Radial jitter disc radius in studs Weight	number	1	Base selection weight before the cumulative-inverse falloff  Points are visually editable in Studio — add, remove, or move an attachment and the spawner picks it up immediately (the cache is rebuilt on first use per group, and a CollectionService.GetInstanceRemovedSignal listener invalidates the group if the root model is untagged or removed).

searchDocs.title: EnemyAssets folder​
searchDocs.content: Enemy Model assets live in ServerStorage/EnemyAssets/. Each child Model must have:  A Humanoid (authoritative stats are applied at spawn time from the archetype config, but the Humanoid must exist for health/death tracking)A PrimaryPart or HumanoidRootPart (used for pivot placement and SpawnVerification spacing tests)  At module load, EnemySpawnerConfig validates every archetype's Model name against EnemyAssets children and emits a warn for any missing model. Building before art is ready is fully supported: register a placeholder dummy (any Model with a Humanoid) in EnemyAssets under the expected name.

searchDocs.title: Public API​
searchDocs.content: EnemySpawner is a server-only module (ServerStorage/SharedModules/EnemySpawner.luau). Call EnemySpawner.Init() once from the system loader before using the rest of the API.  EnemySpawner.Init()   Called once by EnemySpawnerSystemLoader.server.luau at server start. Creates workspace.ActiveEnemies if absent and wires the group-cache invalidation listener.    EnemySpawner.SpawnWave(groupName: string, request: SpawnRequest): WaveHandle   Spawns request.count enemies across the named group's points using the selection algorithm below. composition is either a single archetype name ("PirateGrunt") or a weighted table ({ PirateGrunt = 3, PirateBrute = 1 }) — the weight table is rolled per enemy. If request.interval > 0, spawns are staggered in a task.spawn loop (drip-feed); the WaveHandle is returned immediately and OnCleared waits for both all spawns to be attempted and all registered enemies to die. If request.seed is set, the internal Random is re-seeded for deterministic reproduction.  export type SpawnRequest = { count: number, composition: string | { [string]: number }, interval: number?, -- seconds between spawns; nil/0 = all at once seed: number?, -- optional deterministic RNG seed }     EnemySpawner.SpawnAt(groupName: string, pointName: string, archetypeName: string): Model?   Direct escape hatch: place exactly one archetype at the named attachment (matched by Attachment.Name), still subject to verification. Returns the placed Model or nil if verification fails after MaxRetries or the point/archetype is not found.    EnemySpawner.ResetGroup(groupName: string)   Clears the group's cumulative per-point spawn counts. Call this at the start of each new encounter so point weighting begins fresh. Deaths do not reduce a point's count; only ResetGroup does.

searchDocs.title: Per-enemy spawn algorithm​
searchDocs.content: For each enemy in a wave the spawner runs:  Select a point — weighted random over the group's EnemySpawnPoint attachments. Effective weight is point.Weight / (cumulativeCount + 1) ^ WeightFalloff, where cumulativeCount is the number of enemies spawned from that point this encounter. Points that have spawned fewer enemies this encounter are proportionally more likely; a point with count 0 carries its full base weight. Counts are per-encounter — ResetGroup resets them; enemy deaths do not. Jitter — candidate position = point world position + a uniform random offset within a disc of the point's Radius on the XZ plane. The disc uses sqrt(NextNumber()) * radius so the distribution is uniform over the area rather than biased toward the centre. Verify — the candidate is passed to SpawnVerification with the archetype's body size, an ignore list containing the group model and the ActiveEnemies folder, and the current list of living enemies. Retry-then-skip — steps 2–3 repeat up to Verification.MaxRetries times. If no valid position is found, the enemy is skipped (a warn is emitted) and the wave continues. The wave never hard-fails; it never places a broken enemy. Place — if the global cap (GLOBAL_MAX_ENEMIES) is already met, the enemy is skipped with a warn. Otherwise the archetype Model is cloned from ServerStorage.EnemyAssets, archetype stats are applied (Humanoid.MaxHealth/Health/WalkSpeed), the model is tagged EnemyNPC (or FriendlyNPC if archetype.Faction == "Friendly") so Factions resolves it for CombatService and NpcCollisionService, the model is pivoted to the verified ground-snapped CFrame, parented to workspace.ActiveEnemies, and the point's cumulative count is incremented. The spawned model is registered with the wave handle, and Signals.OnEnemySpawned fires with the placed position and archetype name.

searchDocs.title: SpawnVerification​
searchDocs.content: SpawnVerification (ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/SpawnVerification.luau) is a stateless pure-geometry validator with no server-only dependencies. It lives in SharedModules so it is independently testable and reusable from a future client-side preview. All v1 callers are server-side.  SpawnVerification.Verify( candidate: Vector3, bodySize: Vector3, ignoreList: { Instance }, livingEnemies: { Model } ): VerifyResult -- { ok: boolean, position: Vector3?, reason: string? }   Checks are run cheapest-first with short-circuit on failure:  Ground below — workspace:Raycast straight down from candidate + (0, 2, 0) up to MaxGroundDrop studs, excluding ignoreList. No hit returns { ok = false, reason = "void" }. On hit, the Y position is snapped to the floor: snapped.Y = hit.Position.Y + bodySize.Y / 2. Clear of walls / headroom — workspace:GetPartBoundsInBox of HeadroomSize centred on the snapped position, excluding ignoreList. Any solid collidable part returns { ok = false, reason = "blocked" }. This catches both embedded-in-wall and under-floor cases. Spacing — if any model in livingEnemies has its pivot within MinEnemySpacing studs of the snapped position, returns { ok = false, reason = "crowded" }.  A successful check returns { ok = true, position = snapped } where position is the ground-snapped placement CFrame origin.

searchDocs.title: WaveHandle lifecycle​
searchDocs.content: SpawnWave returns a WaveHandle backed by a Janitor. The handle tracks every spawned enemy's death and removal.  export type WaveHandle = { OnCleared: Signal<()>, -- fires once: all enemies dead AND wave complete GetAlive: (self) -> number, -- count of enemies still alive GetEnemies: (self) -> { Model }, -- list of enemies still alive Despawn: (self) -> (), -- destroy remaining enemies + remove from tracking Destroy: (self) -> (), -- Despawn + Janitor teardown }   Each spawned enemy's Humanoid.Died and AncestryChanged (for despawn-without-death) are connected via the handle's Janitor. OnCleared fires once when the alive count reaches zero and the wave has been marked complete (all drip-feed spawns attempted). Killing enemies before the last drip-feed slot fires will not trigger OnCleared prematurely.  Typical orchestrator pattern:  local wave = EnemySpawner.SpawnWave("PirateShip", { count = 6, composition = { PirateGrunt = 3, PirateBrute = 1 }, interval = 0.5, }) wave.OnCleared:Connect(function() resumeEncounter() end)   Despawn lets an orchestrator abort a wave early (encounter cancelled, train resumes) and cleanly destroy remaining enemies. Calling Despawn when all enemies are already dead is safe (no-op). Destroy implies Despawn and additionally tears down the Janitor, disconnecting all event connections.

searchDocs.content: File	Rolesrc/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/EnemySpawnerConfig.luau	Archetype registry, global tuning constants, Verification.* knobs; validates model names against ServerStorage.EnemyAssets at load src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/SpawnVerification.luau	Stateless ground/wall/spacing validator; returns a ground-snapped position on success src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/EnemyWave.luau	WaveHandle factory: Janitor-backed enemy tracker, OnCleared signal, Despawn/Destroy src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/EnemySpawner.luau	Server service: group registry, point selection, jitter, placement, SpawnWave/SpawnAt/ResetGroup, drip-feed scheduling, global cap src/ServerScriptService/EnemySpawnerSystemLoader.server.luau	Thin bootstrap: calls EnemySpawner.Init() once per server src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Signals/init.luau	Contains OnEnemySpawned signal registration

searchDocs.title: Config knobs​
searchDocs.content: All tuning lives in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/EnemySpawnerConfig.luau. The module is accessible from both client and server; the archetype validation block is guarded by RunService:IsServer() since ServerStorage is inaccessible on the client.  Field	Default	EffectGLOBAL_MAX_ENEMIES	40	Hard cap on total active enemies across all groups. Exceeding the cap skips spawns with a warn. Lower temporarily to verify the cap in Studio. DEFAULT_POINT_RADIUS	6	Fallback jitter disc radius (studs) when neither the point Radius attribute nor the archetype DefaultRadius is set. WeightFalloff	1.0	Exponent k in effectiveWeight = baseWeight / (count + 1) ^ k. At 1.0 weight halves each time a point is used. Raise to flatten selection (less adaptive); lower toward 0 to disable cumulative penalisation. Verification.MaxGroundDrop	25	Maximum downward raycast distance (studs) to find a floor below the candidate. Candidates with no solid ground within this distance are rejected as "void". Verification.HeadroomSize	Vector3.new(3, 6, 3)	Box dimensions used for the wall/headroom overlap check centred on the snapped candidate. Should match or slightly exceed the tallest enemy body. Verification.MinEnemySpacing	4	Minimum distance (studs) between a new candidate and any already-living enemy pivot. Candidates closer than this are rejected as "crowded". Verification.MaxRetries	8	Number of jitter re-rolls before an enemy is skipped with a warn. Higher values increase spawn success at the cost of time per enemy. Archetypes	(see below)	Per-archetype table: Model (child name in EnemyAssets), Health, WalkSpeed, DefaultRadius, optional Faction ("Enemy" / "Friendly"; defaults to "Enemy").

searchDocs.title: Archetype example​
searchDocs.content: EnemySpawnerConfig.Archetypes = { PirateGrunt = { Model = "PirateGrunt", Health = 100, WalkSpeed = 14, DefaultRadius = 6 }, PirateBrute = { Model = "PirateBrute", Health = 300, WalkSpeed = 10, DefaultRadius = 4 }, }   Adding a new archetype: add an entry here, create the corresponding Model in ServerStorage/EnemyAssets/, and the spawner picks it up at next load. No code changes elsewhere are needed.

searchDocs.title: EnemySpawnGroup model​
searchDocs.content: Select any Model in the workspace (pirate ship, outpost, or a plain wrapped Part).Tag it EnemySpawnGroup via the Studio Tag Editor (or CollectionService:AddTag).Optionally set a GroupName string attribute on the model root. If absent, model.Name is used.

searchDocs.title: EnemySpawnPoint attachments​
searchDocs.content: Under the group model, insert one or more Attachment instances:  Insert an Attachment anywhere in the model hierarchy (directly on a Part, inside a nested model, etc.).Tag it EnemySpawnPoint.Optionally add a Radius (number) attribute for this point's jitter disc.Optionally add a Weight (number) attribute to bias selection toward or away from this point.  The attachment's position in Studio is the spawn point's world-space origin at runtime. Move attachments freely; the spawner reads .WorldPosition live at spawn time.

searchDocs.title: EnemyAssets folder​
searchDocs.content: In Studio, create a folder named EnemyAssets inside ServerStorage. Under it, place enemy Models. Each model must have a Humanoid and a PrimaryPart (or HumanoidRootPart). The name of the model must match the Model field in the corresponding archetype entry in EnemySpawnerConfig.Archetypes.  Minimum viable setup for testing before art is ready:  Insert a default Roblox Dummy (rig_type = R15 or R6) into ServerStorage/EnemyAssets/.Rename it to PirateGrunt.The archetype validation at load will stop warning; SpawnWave will clone the dummy.

searchDocs.title: Collision and combat wiring​
searchDocs.content: No additional Studio wiring is required for collision passthrough or combat. Spawned enemies are tagged EnemyNPC (or FriendlyNPC), and:  NpcCollisionService adds them to the Character collision group so players pass through them.CombatService.ApplyToModel resolves them via Factions so weapon hits deal damage.  Both services detect the tags automatically on CollectionService.GetInstanceAddedSignal.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: WaveHandle OnCleared requires both conditions OnCleared fires only when the alive count is zero AND all drip-feed spawns have been attempted (MarkComplete has been called internally). In an instant wave (interval = 0) this means OnCleared can fire during SpawnWave itself, before it returns, if no enemies are placed (e.g. every enemy was skipped). Always set up OnCleared connections before calling SpawnWave, or use the returned handle and do not assume it is deferred.  Cumulative counts survive across waves; ResetGroup does not EnemySpawner.ResetGroup(groupName) resets the per-point counts for the named group so point selection begins fresh. If you call SpawnWave a second time without resetting, previously-used points start at a cumulative disadvantage. For repeating encounter patterns (waves 1, 2, 3…), decide explicitly whether to reset between waves or let cumulative weighting carry across the full encounter.  GLOBAL_MAX_ENEMIES counts workspace.ActiveEnemies children The cap is the live child count of workspace.ActiveEnemies. If enemies are not parented there (e.g. manually cloned models outside the spawner), they do not count toward the cap, which may allow over-cap situations. Always spawn enemies through EnemySpawner; do not manually parent enemy models into ActiveEnemies.  SpawnVerification is in SharedModules but is server-only in v1 SpawnVerification is in ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/ so it has no server-only dependencies and can be used from a future client-side preview (e.g. displaying valid spawn zones in a director tool). In v1, all calls happen server-side via EnemySpawner. Do not call it on the client in production without auditing the ignoreList and livingEnemies arguments for client-visible data.  Archetype validation warns but does not error If a model is missing from EnemyAssets at load time, EnemySpawnerConfig emits a warn but does not error. The spawner itself will also warn (and skip the enemy) at spawn time if the model is still absent. Register placeholder models early to keep the Output clean during development.

searchDocs.title: Future directions​
searchDocs.content: Off-screen spawn preference — an additional weighting term in step 1 of the selection algorithm that demotes EnemySpawnPoints currently inside any player's camera frustum. Enemies would appear from behind cover or at the edge of vision. The term slots into the effective-weight formula without changing the rest of the algorithm.Reachability pre-check — PathfindingService:CreatePath from the verified candidate position to the nearest player, rejecting candidates in sealed-off areas. This is the deferred line-of-sight check in SpawnVerification, done properly. Build alongside the enemy pathfinding AI system.Encounter director — a layer above the spawner that scales count/composition/interval by wave number, player count, or Tech Tree progress. The spawner stays a dumb placement service; the director owns escalation and pacing. Lives as a separate module; EnemySpawner requires no changes.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: Server (HealthManager) Client (HealthController) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── PlayerAdded → create HealthRecord{ Health = MaxHealth, LastDamageTime = 0, LastSyncTime = 0, LastSyncedHealth = MaxHealth } CharacterAdded → reset Health to MaxHealth humanoid.MaxHealth = HealthConfig.MaxHealth humanoid.Health = record.Health ──── HealthStateSync:FireClient(player, health) ──────► Packets.HealthStateSync .OnClientEvent → Signals.OnHealthValueChanged :Fire(health) │ ▼ HealthStaminaGuiController (drives health bar) RunService.Heartbeat (server): if regen eligible (alive, not full, past RegenDelay): record.Health += HealthRegen * dt humanoid.Health = record.Health if periodicSync (0.1 s) or full: ──── HealthStateSync:FireClient ─────────────────► HealthManager.ApplyDamage: validate AttackType / AOEVariant clamp amount to [0, MaxHealth] amount *= (1 - clamp(ArmorBaseReduction * (1 + ArmorEfficiency), 0, 0.75)) -- crafted armor x Armor perk record.Health -= amount record.LastDamageTime = os.clock() humanoid.Health = record.Health ──── HealthStateSync:FireClient ─────────────────────► HealthManager.HealPlayer: record.Health = min(MaxHealth, record.Health + amount) humanoid.Health = record.Health ──── HealthStateSync:FireClient ─────────────────────►

searchDocs.title: Client / Server / Shared​
searchDocs.content: Client (HealthController.client.luau)Minimal bridge: listens to Packets.HealthStateSync.OnClientEvent and re-fires Signals.OnHealthValueChanged with the received health value. It owns no state. HealthStaminaGuiController (not part of this system) consumes OnHealthValueChanged to animate the HUD bar.  Server (HealthManager.luau)Bootstrapped by HealthSystemLoader.server.luau via HealthManager.Initialize(). Maintains a HealthRecord per player (Health, LastDamageTime, LastSyncTime, LastSyncedHealth). The regen heartbeat is capped at MAX_HEALTH_STEP_DT = 0.1 seconds per step to prevent delta-time spikes from applying burst healing. Syncs are batched: regen fires HealthStateSync at most every HEALTH_SYNC_INTERVAL = 0.1 seconds, or immediately when health reaches full. On PlayerRemoving the record is deleted; no stale data persists across sessions.  Shared (HealthConfig.luau)Three fields read by both HealthManager (server logic) and indirectly by HealthController/GUI (via the synced value): MaxHealth, HealthRegen, RegenDelay. RegenEnabled is a kill-switch for the entire regen loop.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Non-CombatService damage bypasses HealthManager HealthManager.ApplyDamage is now called by CombatService (which WeaponServer and NpcCollisionService route through). However, any damage source that writes directly to Humanoid.Health — such as default Roblox fall damage or unrouted hazards — will bypass HealthManager's internal record, causing the HUD to show a stale value and skipping armor mitigation. Before shipping such a source, either disable it or listen to Humanoid.HealthChanged and reconcile the record (see audit note H3 in the source).  One-way mirror: HealthManager writes record.Health → humanoid.Health but never reads back from the Humanoid. Any external write to humanoid.Health is invisible to the manager until a HealthStateSync event corrects the client. Keep all health mutations going through HealthManager.ApplyDamage or HealthManager.HealPlayer.  Armor mitigation: applyDamageInternal combines crafted armor with the Armor perk as the final scale on amount before health is subtracted. It reads ArmorState/<UserId>.ArmorBaseReduction (written by ArmorManager from the player's tier) and PerkBuffs/<UserId>.ArmorEfficiency (the Armor perk), computing reduction = clamp(ArmorBaseReduction * (1 + ArmorEfficiency), 0, ArmorConfig.MaxReductionCap). Both are read per hit, so crafting a tier or allocating/respeccing the perk takes effect on the next damage event; with no armor the perk does nothing. Coverage is bounded by the chokepoint — damage that bypasses HealthManager.ApplyDamage also bypasses armor. See Perks for the cap rationale and the attacker-bonus-then-armor multiplication order.  Character respawn resets health: CharacterAdded unconditionally resets record.Health to MaxHealth. If a partial-health respawn mechanic is ever needed, this reset must be conditional.  Sync rate: HealthStateSync is sent at most every 0.1 seconds during regen. For combat situations where granular damage feedback matters, callers to ApplyDamage should be aware that each call forces an immediate sync — avoid calling it in tight per-frame loops.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: Any client script fires: Signals.RequestNotification:Fire(type, message, duration?, executedFunction?) └─> NotificationManager (sole subscriber) ├─ validate type against NotificationConfig.Types ├─ enforce MaxConcurrent cap (evict oldest non-executed toast if needed) ├─ build Frame in NotificationGui.MainContainer │ ├─ icon ImageLabel (per-type asset ID + color from NotificationConfig) │ ├─ time-left bar (timed toasts only; linear MotionMaster tween) │ └─ text label with gradient-sweep reveal ├─ SoundManager.PlaySFX(NotificationConfig.SfxNames[type]) ├─ intro animations via MotionMaster (size expand + fade in) └─ schedule close: ├─ timed: task.delay(duration or Device.Duration, closeEntry) └─> executed: task.spawn(executedFunction) -> closeEntry on return (optional ExecutedFunctionTimeout safety close) Signals.RequestClearNotifications:Fire() └─> closeEntry() on all active toasts simultaneously

searchDocs.title: Client / Server / Shared​
searchDocs.content: The notification system is client-only. There is no server component.  NotificationController.client.luau  A three-line bootstrap that calls NotificationManager.Init() once. After Init runs, NotificationManager subscribes to Signals.RequestNotification and Signals.RequestClearNotifications. No other setup is required.  NotificationManager/init.luau  Manages the full toast lifecycle:  Creates (lazily) a ScreenGui named NotificationGui with a UIListLayout container anchored to the top-centre of the screen. The top offset is NotificationConfig.TopOffsetScale (a fraction of viewport height). New toasts are inserted at the top of the stack; LayoutOrder is a negated monotonic counter so newer toasts sort above older ones.Executed-function toasts (executedFunction ~= nil) sit above timed toasts in a reserved LayoutOrder band.Font size and padding are viewport-responsive: scaled by math.min(viewport.X, viewport.Y) / BaseScreenMin, clamped to [0.7, 1.3].Text width is measured via TextService:GetTextSize after accounting for icon width, time-bar width (timed toasts only), and padding gaps, so the label never clips its content.Close animations run a MotionMaster tween that shrinks the frame to UDim2.fromOffset(0, 0); the Janitor per entry destroys the frame when the tween completes.A debounced viewport resize handler (requestResize) re-measures and re-tweens all live toasts when the window size changes.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Use Signals — never require NotificationManager directly Feature controllers must fire Signals.RequestNotification:Fire(type, message, duration?, executedFunction?) to show a toast. Requiring NotificationManager directly and calling internal functions breaks the decoupled contract, creates a hard dependency on a client-only module, and will error if accidentally required server-side.  type must exactly match one of the five lowercase strings in NotificationConfig.Types. An unrecognised type is silently dropped (no toast, no error).duration overrides the device default (NotificationConfig.Device.Desktop.Duration or .Mobile.Duration). Pass nil to use the default.Passing executedFunction makes the toast persist until the function returns (or ExecutedFunctionTimeout elapses). The function runs in a pcall-protected task.spawn — errors are suppressed and the toast still closes. Keep the function short; it runs on the client main thread.When MaxConcurrent is reached, the oldest timed toast is force-closed. Executed-function toasts are never evicted by the cap — they stay until their function returns. Avoid queuing many long-running executed toasts simultaneously.Signals.RequestClearNotifications:Fire() closes all active toasts immediately regardless of type or remaining duration. Use it only for hard resets (e.g. character death, scene transitions).

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: JunkService (server) — spawn loop • selectRandomJunk() — weighted tier + pity type selection • assigns id (U16), records SpawnOdometer + SpawnPos • SpawnJunk:Fire(id, modelName, startPos) ──────────────────────────► JunkController (client) • pools[poolName]:RetrieveObject(startPos) • adds to activeJunks + junkMap SetJunkSpeed:Fire(targetSpeed) ─────────────────────────────────────► JunkController (client) (on train state change or player join) • first receipt: snap currentSpeed • subsequent: start smoothstep ramp ┌── Shared speed ramp (same smoothstep on both sides) ──────────────────────────────┐ │ JunkService Heartbeat: junkOdometer += currentSpeed * dt │ │ JunkController PreSimulation: advance each junk's DistanceTraveled │ │ Despawn when (junkOdometer - SpawnOdometer) > DESPAWN_DISTANCE (server) │ │ when DistanceTraveled > DESPAWN_DISTANCE (client) │ └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ Player fires GrabHook → Signals.TryClaimJunk:Fire(id, hitPos) • JunkController → Packets.ReqJunkClaim:Fire(id, hitPos) ──────────► JunkService • proximity check vs junkOdometer • cooldown check • reserves junk for player • BeginJunkRetract:Fire(id, hitPos, retractTime, player) ◄── BeginJunkRetract ─────────────────────────────────────────────── • remove from activeJunks; move to retractingJunks • if localPlayer: GrabHookVisuals.AnimateProjectile drives movement • if other player: observer lerp on RenderStepped Player fires Signals.TryFinalizeJunk:Fire(id) • JunkController → Packets.ReqJunkFinalize:Fire(id) ───────────────► JunkService • verifies reservation + timeout • marks Collected, awards Tool to Backpack • JunkCollected:Fire(id, player) → all clients ◄── JunkCollected ────────────────────────────────────────────────── • pool:InsertObject (returns model)

searchDocs.title: Client / Server / Shared​
searchDocs.content: Client (JunkController.client.luau)  Builds per-model GenericPoolInstance pools at startup, one per model name found in JunkAssets, with initial size 5, max 60, expand by 10.On SpawnJunk: checks MAX_CLIENT_JUNKS = 250 cap, retrieves model from pool, sets Transparency = 0, parents to workspace/JunksVisuals, records in activeJunks and junkMap.PreSimulation loop: advances the smoothstep speed ramp, moves each active junk by currentSpeed * dt along MOVE_DIRECTION, applies per-junk random rotation, increments DistanceTraveled. Despawns via RemoveJunkLocal when DistanceTraveled > DESPAWN_DISTANCE.On BeginJunkRetract: removes the junk from simulation, moves it to retractingJunks. The local player's animation is driven by GrabHookVisuals.AnimateProjectile; other players see an observer lerp on RenderStepped. An 8-second safety-net timeout returns the model to the pool if JunkCollected never arrives.On JunkCollected: cleans up rope attachments and beams on the model, returns it to the pool.Bridges claim/finalize signals from GrabHook.client to Packets.ReqJunkClaim / Packets.ReqJunkFinalize via Signals.TryClaimJunk and Signals.TryFinalizeJunk.Exposes GetJunkIdFromPart(part) via BindableCore so GrabHook.client can resolve a junk ID from a raycast hit part.  Server (JunkService.server.luau)  Weighted tier selection: each tier's weight is multiplied by GlobalModifiers.TierMultipliers[tier]; a random number selects the tier by accumulated weight.Type selection with pity: if spawnsSinceLastEnergy >= ENERGY_PITY_THRESHOLD (8), an Energy type junk is forced; otherwise weighted by SpawnChance * TypeMultiplier. The pity counter resets on every Energy spawn.Records SpawnOdometer (value of junkOdometer at spawn time) and SpawnPos for each active junk. The junk's current world position is reconstructed on claim as SpawnPos + MOVE_DIRECTION * (junkOdometer - SpawnOdometer).Distance-based despawn on Heartbeat: removes any junk where (junkOdometer - SpawnOdometer) > DESPAWN_DISTANCE. This mirrors the client-side DistanceTraveled check.Claim validation (ReqJunkClaim): reconstructs junk world position, checks distance against GrabHookConfig.Physics.MaxDistance + 15 studs (latency slack), enforces per-player cooldown, reserves junk, computes retract time, and fires BeginJunkRetract to all clients.Finalize validation (ReqJunkFinalize): checks reservation ownership and 5-second timeout, marks collected, fires JunkCollected to all clients, and gives the tool to the player's Backpack.SetTrainState(isMoving) and SetTrainStarted(started) are wired to Signals.SetTrainState and Signals.SetTrainStarted for external control.Junk counter wraps at 65535 (U16 boundary) to keep IDs compact in the SpawnJunk packet.  Shared (SpawnHelper.luau)  SpawnHelper:Init() caches all BasePart children of workspace/SpawnVolumes weighted by volume.SpawnHelper.GetRandomPoint() picks a random world position inside one of the spawn volumes using volume-weighted selection.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Both sides integrate the same ramp — keep them in sync The server (junkOdometer) and client (DistanceTraveled) both use the identical smoothstep ramp over SPEED_RAMP_DURATION. If you change the ramp formula in one place, change it in the other. Drift causes the server's proximity check to reject valid claims.  Reservation timeout is 5 seconds If a client claims junk but never finalizes (e.g. disconnects mid-retract), the reservation expires after 5 seconds (RESERVATION_TIMEOUT). Another player can then claim the same junk. The client has an 8-second safety net (RETRACT_RECLAIM_TIMEOUT) that returns the model to the pool if JunkCollected never arrives — this value must exceed RESERVATION_TIMEOUT plus round-trip time.  Pool cleanup is mandatory. Every path that removes a junk from activeJunks or retractingJunks must call CleanupJunkModel then pool:InsertObject. Skipping cleanup leaks HookAttachment or Beam instances on the model, which will appear on the next retrieval.workspace/JunksVisuals folder must exist. JunkController uses WaitForChild to find it; the folder should be created in the place file or by a server startup script.Junk ID wraps at 65535. This is intentional for the NumberU16 wire type in SpawnJunk. Long-running servers are safe because entries are removed before the counter can collide.Tier 5 weight is 0. Items in Tier 5 will never spawn under default config. Set the weight above 0 to enable them.SpawnHelper:Init() must be called before the spawn loop. JunkService calls it at startup; if no SpawnVolumes parts exist in workspace, GetRandomPoint will always return nil and no junk will spawn.

searchDocs.title: Point economy​
searchDocs.content: Each level-up grants 1 Personal point AND 1 Party point.Available points = playerLevel - sum(spent in that pool).Points cannot go negative; the pool is floored at 0.Respec costs nothing and returns all points in the chosen pool.Points carry across places because PerkManager uses the same DataStore key (PlayerPerks) everywhere in the universe.

searchDocs.title: Party-max resolution​
searchDocs.content: Party perks (Salvage Luck, Fuel Efficiency, Thrift, Shield Capacity, Heavy Ordnance) apply to the entire server, but only the highest level held by any single player is active. If Player A has Salvage Luck 6 and Player B has Salvage Luck 3, the server resolves at 6. PerkEffectsDispatcher recomputes the max on every allocate, respec, player join, and player leave.

searchDocs.title: Buff contract​
searchDocs.content: PerkEffectsDispatcher is the sole writer of the buff folders. Other systems read only — never write.  Folder	Scope	Updated whenReplicatedStorage/PerkBuffs/<UserId>	Personal, per-player	On allocate/respec, player join, player leave ReplicatedStorage/PartyPerkBuffs	Party, server-max	Same as above  Attribute keys match PerkConfig.BuffKey:  Perk	BuffKey	Value formula	ConsumerVitality	HPBonus	0.04 * level	HealthManager Regeneration	RegenBonus	0.10 * level	HealthManager Quick Reel	ReelSpeedBonus	0.05 * level	GrabHook Power	DamageBonus	0.03 * level	WeaponServer (chokepoint: scaledDamage, applied after headshot multiplier, all 5 player-attack sites) Fortune	CoinGainBonus	0.05 * level	CoinManager.AddCoins (math.max(1, math.floor(amount * (1 + bonus))) — 1-coin minimum) Armor	ArmorEfficiency	0.025 * level	HealthManager (chokepoint: applyDamageInternal) — multiplies the crafted-armor base reduction: clamp(ArmorBaseReduction * (1 + ArmorEfficiency), 0, 0.75). No armor equipped ⇒ no reduction. Salvage Luck	JunkTierRarityBonus	0.08 * level	JunkService (via ApplyTierMultiplier) Efficiency	FuelEfficiencyBonus	0.04 * level	TrainFuelManager drain multiplier — stacks multiplicatively with TechTreeBuffs.FuelEfficiency (see Tech Tree) Thrift	WeaponCostReduction	0.03 * level	(deferred — no weapon cost mechanic exists; declared in config, intentionally unwired) Shield Capacity	TrainShieldBonus	0.05 * level	TrainShieldManager.recomputeMax — multiplicative on top of BASE_SHIELD + TechTreeBuffs.MaxHP; see Train Shield Heavy Ordnance	CannonDamageBonus	0.06 * level	CannonServer (applyCannonAOE, applied as Damage × (1 + CannonDamageBonus) per shot). Consumed by the Cannon system at the server shell-damage line.  Perks marked (deferred) have no planned consumer yet.  Armor damage mitigation. Crafted armor (see ArmorConfig / ArmorManager) publishes a per-player ArmorState/<UserId>.ArmorBaseReduction — the base fraction of incoming damage removed by the player's current armor tier. The Armor perk no longer reduces damage on its own; it is an efficiency multiplier on that base. HealthManager.applyDamageInternal reads both per hit and computes reduction = clamp(ArmorBaseReduction * (1 + ArmorEfficiency), 0, 0.75), then scales amount by (1 - reduction) as the final step before subtracting from health. With no armor (tier 0 → base 0) the perk contributes nothing. Because the attacker's DamageBonus is already applied upstream in WeaponServer, attacker bonus and defender mitigation multiply independently: base * (1 + DamageBonus) * (1 - reduction). Coverage is every path routed through CombatService/HealthManager (Melee/Bullet/AOE and NPC hits); damage written directly to Humanoid.Health bypasses the sink and is not mitigated (see Health).

searchDocs.title: Client / Server / Shared​
searchDocs.content: Shared — PerkConfig.luau is the single tuning surface: 11 perk declarations with Category, BuffKey, PerLevel, MaxLevel, DisplayName, Description, and display Order. Tune values here — do not hard-code them in logic. PerkConfig.STORE_NAME is the ProfileStore key, identical across all places.  Shared — PerkResultCodes.luau is the frozen result-code enum (OK=0, NO_PROFILE=1, UNKNOWN_PERK=2, AT_MAX_LEVEL=3, NO_POINTS=4). Used by both the server handler and the client UI.  Shared — PerkState.luau is a pure, side-effect-free module with three functions: spent(perkLevels, category), available(perkLevels, category, playerLevel), and canAllocate(perkLevels, perkId, playerLevel). The server uses it for authoritative validation; the client uses it to gate the + button.  Server — PerkManager.luau owns the PlayerPerks ProfileStore (one session per player). AllocatePoint and Respec validate, mutate PerkLevels, fire OnPerkStateChanged, and replicate. Initialize wires PlayerAdded, PlayerRemoving, packet handlers, and OnPlayerLevelUp re-replicate. GetPerkLevels(player) returns the live reference for PerkEffectsDispatcher.  Server — PerkSystemLoader.server.luau calls PerkManager.Initialize() once per server.  Server — PerkEffectsDispatcher.server.luau is the sole writer of both buff folders. It listens to OnPerkStateChanged, PlayerAdded, and PlayerRemoving, then calls publishPersonal (per-player attributes) and publishParty (server-max across all players). Also bridges Junk Rarity to Signals.ApplyTierMultiplier (which JunkService already consumes).  Client — PerkClient.luau is the GUI-agnostic data layer (owns no GUI). It caches the authoritative PerkStateSync snapshot, watches the replicated PartyPerkBuffs folder, and exposes queries returning PerkView descriptors (GetPerks/GetActivePerks/GetAvailablePoints/GetPerk), commands with optimistic prediction (Allocate/Respec/CanRespec), and a Changed signal. "Active" is category-aware: a Personal perk is active at the player's Level > 0; a Party perk is active at its server-wide ActivePartyLevel > 0. Perk screens are authored separately, require PerkClient, and subscribe to Changed to repaint.  Client — PerkController.client.luau is a one-line bootstrap that calls PerkClient.Init() once on join so the data layer is warm before any GUI opens.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Points are derived, not stored PerkLevels is the only persisted data. Available points = level - spent. Never add a separate stored point counter — it will desync.  Party perk levels shown in the GUI are per-player, not the resolved active level The + button and level display in the Party tab show how many points this player has invested. The (active N) sub-label shows the server-resolved max. Both are expected: a player at level 3 in a party where someone else is at level 7 sees Lv 3/10 (active 7).  PerkEffectsDispatcher must run before PerkManager on join PerkEffectsDispatcher seeds its folder at boot. PerkManager fires OnPerkStateChanged after profile load, which triggers a republish. The ordering is correct because both are ServerScriptService scripts and PerkManager.Initialize() is called from PerkSystemLoader, which yields on ProfileStore:StartSessionAsync before firing the signal.  HPBonus subscription attaches once at join HealthManager subscribes to the HPBonus attribute change in PlayerAdded, not CharacterAdded. If PerkBuffs/<UserId> does not exist at join time (the dispatcher hasn't seeded yet), the subscription is skipped for that session. In practice the dispatcher seeds synchronously at boot, so the folder exists before any player's PlayerAdded fires normally.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: Player presses MoveButton / StashButton (GUI) └─> PlaceableActions.bind() fires ReqMovePlaceable / ReqStashPlaceable packet └─> PlaceableActionsServer.OnServerInvoke ├─ cooldown check (per-player, os.clock) ├─ ancestry check (model.Parent == workspace.PlacedObjects) ├─ attribute check (PlaceableName attribute on model) ├─ tool template check (ReplicatedStorage.PlaceableTools/<Name>) ├─ proximity check (HRP distance <= MaxActionDistance) ├─ atomic claim (model.Parent = nil, race guard) ├─ clone Tool -> player.Backpack ├─ Move only: humanoid:EquipTool(newTool) ├─ BroadcastPlaceablePoof:Fire(cframe, placeableName, isMove) └─ model:Destroy() + record cooldown timestamp └─> All clients receive poof broadcast └─> PlaceableActions (client) plays shrink tween + SFX

searchDocs.title: Client / Server / Shared​
searchDocs.content: Shared — PlaceableActions.luau  PlaceableActions.bind(model, gui) wires MoveButton and StashButton into the packet system and returns a Binding with a single Unbind() method. On success the module fires Signals.OnPlaceableMoved or Signals.OnPlaceableStashed so other systems can react without polling.  The poof handler is also client-only and lives in this file. On receiving BroadcastPlaceablePoof it clones the matching model from ReplicatedStorage.PlaceableItems, strips scripts/collisions/shadows from the clone, parents it to workspace.PlaceablePoofs, then runs a parallel MotionMaster.Sequence that shrinks every BasePart to near-zero while fading it out. The clone self-destructs when the sequence completes.  Server — PlaceableActionsServer.server.luau  Owns the OnServerInvoke handlers for ReqStashPlaceable and ReqMovePlaceable. Runs every validation step listed in the data-flow diagram. The atomic claim pattern (model.Parent = nil followed by a re-read) prevents two simultaneous requests from granting the same item twice. Returns boolean — false on any failed check, true on full success.  On a successful Move, the handler also calls PlaceableRevertStore.Set(player, { cframe = cframe, placeableName = placeableName, tool = newTool }), recording the item's original CFrame under the granted tool instance. This lets the build-mode cancel (RequestPlacementRevert) revert the item to its original spot if the player presses X without re-placing. The entry is cleared when the player re-places via PlaceItem, when the revert fires and consumes it, or when the player leaves the server.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Three requirements must all be present A placeable supports Stash/Move only when all three of the following exist simultaneously: A Model in ReplicatedStorage/PlaceableItems/<Name> (already required for placement).A Tool template in ReplicatedStorage/PlaceableTools/<Name> with a PlaceableName attribute set to the same name string.ImageButton instances named exactly MoveButton and StashButton somewhere inside the GUI that PlaceableActions.bind is called with. Either may be omitted, but the missing one will log a warning and that action will be silently unavailable to the player. If PlaceableTools/<Name> is missing the server returns false and nothing is destroyed — no item is lost — but the player gets no feedback.  The server proximity check (MaxActionDistance) is a second guard independent of the ProximityPrompt range. Keep them in sync when tuning the in-world prompt.Stash/Move discards all per-instance state on the placed model. The granted Tool is always a fresh clone from the template. If per-instance state matters, snapshot attributes before the action reaches the server.Any nearby player can stash any placement — ownership is not tracked. Add per-instance owner attributes and an ownership check in handleAction if griefing becomes a concern.Call binding:Unbind() when the GUI closes. Failing to unbind leaves the Janitor alive and button listeners connected to a GUI that may already be gone.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: Player equips tool │ ▼ PlacementClient (client) • SetBuildMode(true) • SetGhostModel(template) • fires ClientToggleGhost ──────────────────► PlacementServer (server) • validates itemName exists • relays ServerToggleGhost → other clients • Heartbeat: CalculatePlacement (raycast) • UpdateGhostPosition → CheckValidity • fires ClientUpdateGhost (CFrame) ─────────► PlacementServer • type-checks CFrame • relays ServerUpdateGhost → other clients • mouse click / confirm signal • fires PlaceItem (origin, dir, rotation, mode) ► PlacementServer • cooldown check • distance checks (origin + final pos) • isolated PlacementSystem per request • CalculatePlacement + CheckValidity • Clone + finalizeModel → PlacedObjects • destroy tool • ServerToggleGhost(false) → all clients

searchDocs.title: Client / Server / Shared​
searchDocs.content: Client (PlacementClient.client.luau)  Creates one PlacementSystem instance (grid size 2, tag BuildArea).On tool equip: calls SetBuildMode(true), SetGhostModel(template), fires ClientToggleGhost.Fires Signals.RequestShootingCamera(false) on build mode entry to disable the aim camera.Heartbeat loop (rate-limited to GhostUpdateHz, default 20 Hz): raycasts, calls UpdateGhostPosition, fires ClientUpdateGhost with the result CFrame.Fires Signals.OnBuildValidityChanged when validity changes so UI and audio can react.Grid/free toggle, rotation, confirm, cancel, and ghost-lock are all driven by signals wired to BuildModeGuiController.Listens to ServerToggleGhost / ServerUpdateGhost and calls SetOtherGhost to render other players' ghost previews.  Server (PlacementServer.server.luau)  Relays ClientToggleGhost to other players after confirming the item name exists in ReplicatedStorage/PlaceableItems.Relays ClientUpdateGhost (CFrame type-checked) to other players.On PlaceItem: enforces per-player cooldown (PLACE_COOLDOWN = 0.4 s), character/tool guards, ray-origin distance (MAX_ORIGIN_DISTANCE = 50 studs), final-position distance (MAX_PLACE_DISTANCE = 60 studs), and collision validity — all using an isolated PlacementSystem instance with a ServerStorage-parented ghost that is never replicated.On success: clones the template, calls finalizeModel (makes CollisionBox invisible + non-collidable, visual parts opaque, and tags the CollisionBox with PlacementObstruction so future placements collide with it), parents to workspace/PlacedObjects, destroys the player's tool, and broadcasts ghost-clear to all clients.  Shared (PlacementSystem.luau)  Handles ghost model lifecycle, grid-snap vs free-placement position calculation, collision-box derivation, obstruction validity check, and other-player ghost rendering.IS_CLIENT guards prevent Texture and TweenPlus calls from running on the server.SetBuildMode is client-only (creates grid Texture instances on build area parts); the server sets IsBuildMode = true directly.

searchDocs.title: Cancelling build mode​
searchDocs.content: Pressing X (configurable via PlacementConfig.CancelKey) or the on-screen Cancel button (mobile) fires Signals.RequestPlacementCancel. Both paths reach the same cancelPlacement function in PlacementClient, which immediately snaps build-mode visuals off and sends a RequestPlacementRevert RemoteFunction call to the server.  Escape is intentionally not used — Roblox reserves it for the in-game menu.  The server checks PlaceableRevertStore to determine the outcome:  Session type	OutcomeFresh placement (item was never placed before)	Server returns false → client calls humanoid:UnequipTools() and the tool returns to the Backpack Move session, original spot is free	Server re-places the item at its original CFrame, destroys the tool, returns true → item reverts, no unequip needed Move session, original spot is occupied	Server returns false → client falls back to unequip  See Placeable Actions for how a Move session records the revert entry, and the Networking Map for the RequestPlacementRevert packet definition.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Anti-exploit — do not relax the server thresholds MAX_ORIGIN_DISTANCE = 50, MAX_PLACE_DISTANCE = 60, and PLACE_COOLDOWN = 0.4 in PlacementServer are the primary defences against remote placement exploits. Raising these values substantially would allow clients to place items anywhere in the world or spam unlimited items.  Model structure is required. Every entry in ReplicatedStorage/PlaceableItems must have a CollisionBox (BasePart) child. Without it, PlacementSystem warns and falls back to bounding-box collision, which can cause floating or incorrect validity checks.Obstruction is tag-driven, not folder-driven. Build placement only avoids a volume if it is tagged PlacementObstruction. Placed items are tagged automatically on their CollisionBox by finalizeModel. Any static world model that placement must respect (e.g. TrainShieldGeneratorPlaceholder, TechTreeBenchPlaceholder) must have a CollisionBox BasePart tagged PlacementObstruction by hand. Tag the CollisionBox part only, never the whole model — sibling sub-models like TrajectoryPoints would otherwise become map-wide placement blockers.CollisionBox part must not be named RootPart or tagged PlacementIgnore. Those names cause the part to be treated as invisible/non-collidable in the ghost.Each PlaceItem event creates an isolated PlacementSystem. This is intentional — it prevents concurrent requests from different players from corrupting shared state. Do not cache a server-side PlacementSystem across requests.SetBuildMode must only be called on the client. Calling it on the server would create Texture instances in workspace and replicate them to all clients.Ghost relay is observer-only. GhostModels folder and its contents exist only on the client; the server never sees them. The server's validity check correctly skips that folder for this reason.Cutscene and combat gates (isInCutscene, isInCombat) in PlacementClient are not yet wired to any external system — they are TODO integration points.

searchDocs.title: Data model​
searchDocs.content: The profile stores a single value, TotalXP (lifetime cumulative). Level and progress are derived from it via XPCurve.luau, so re-tuning the curve never desyncs saved data.

searchDocs.title: Curve​
searchDocs.content: xpToNext(L) = round(CURVE_COEFF * L ^ CURVE_EXP) + CURVE_OFFSET (defaults5, 1.5, 45), cap MAX_LEVEL = 100. Total to level 100 ≈ 202,000 XP. All constants live in Configs/XPConfig.luau.

searchDocs.title: Earning (party-shared)​
searchDocs.content: XP is shared with the whole party; one party occupies one server, so every player in the server receives the full award.  Distance: while the train is in its "go" state (running — not braked, not stalled), the party earns DISTANCE_XP_PER_TICK every DISTANCE_TICK_SECONDS. Driven off Signals.SetTrainState. The train starts braked, so no XP accrues before the first un-brake.Kills: any EnemyNPC death awards KILL_XP to the party (attribution- agnostic). Wired in XPSystemLoader.

searchDocs.title: Components​
searchDocs.content: Configs/XPConfig.luau — tuning constants.XPCurve.luau — pure level/progress math.XPManager.luau (ServerStorage) — profile lifecycle, award API (AddXP,AddPartyXP), replication. Runs in both places.XPSystemLoader.server.luau — gameplay-only earner wiring.XPController.client.luau — replication bridge → Signals.OnXPChanged, and the level-up toast via Signals.RequestNotification.

searchDocs.title: Cross-place (lobby ↔ gameplay)​
searchDocs.content: DataStores are universe-wide. Both places use the same STORE_NAME and key (tostring(UserId)), so XP/Level are shared automatically; ProfileStore session-locking serializes the teleport handoff. The lobby place must runXPManager.Initialize() and XPController (for display + clean handoff) but NOT XPSystemLoader — no earners in the lobby. The lobby mirror is a separate deployment, not part of this repo.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: Client (ShredderClient) Server (ShredderServer) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── PromptButtonHoldBegan countNonEnergyJunks() > 0 ──── ReqShredderStart(bench) ────► validate: workbench tag, proximity, workbench not locked, cooldown, junk count ShredderMath.ComputeHoldDuration() record session + StartTime ◄── (isValid, duration, code) ─── prompt.HoldDuration = duration PromptButtonHoldEnded → nonce bump (cancels armed session) Prompt.Triggered (hold complete) armedNonce check passes ──── ReqShredderComplete(bench) ──► re-validate: session, workbench match, elapsed >= duration - TOLERANCE, proximity, workbench not locked re-verify junk still owned buildMaterialSequence(junks) destroy junk Tools lock workbench task.spawn(ejectMaterials) ◄── (success, woodCount, metalCount, code) ────────── ejectMaterials(): SplineMove handle P0→arcPeak→landing ProximityPickupServer.RegisterItem() CollectionService tag "CraftMaterial" auto-collect loop (0.5 s poll) unlock workbench after ARC_DURATION Shared: ShredderMath (hold duration), ShredderResultCodes (error enum)

searchDocs.title: Client / Server / Shared​
searchDocs.content: Client (ShredderClient.client.luau)Watches CollectionService for Workbench-tagged models. On each workbench it finds a ProximityPrompts/ShredPromptPart/ProximityPrompt, sets ActionText, HoldDuration, and MaxActivationDistance from config, and wires three connections: PromptButtonHoldBegan (fires ReqShredderStart), PromptButtonHoldEnded (bumps the nonce to cancel), and Triggered (fires ReqShredderComplete only when the nonce matches the armed value). A Backpack and Character Janitor pair keeps HoldDuration in sync whenever junk is added or removed. If the player holds the prompt with zero non-Energy junk, a "info" notification fires and the prompt is briefly disabled.  Server (ShredderServer.server.luau)ReqShredderStart validates the workbench tag, proximity (INTERACT_DISTANCE + INTERACT_DISTANCE_TOLERANCE), workbench lock state, per-player cooldown, and junk availability. It stores a session record (workbench, start time, computed duration, junk snapshot). ReqShredderComplete re-checks all constraints plus timing (elapsed >= duration - HOLD_COMPLETION_TOLERANCE), re-validates junk still belongs to the player from the snapshot, builds a shuffled material sequence, destroys all junk Tools, locks the workbench, then spawns ejectMaterials. Ejection animates each handle along a Catmull-Rom spline (MotionMaster.SplineMove) with uniform-disk scatter around LandingPoint, then calls ProximityPickupServer.RegisterItem. Overflow beyond MAX_ANIMATED_EJECT_ITEMS is granted directly in scheduler batches. A 0.5 s auto-collect loop sweeps droppedMaterials; after AUTO_COLLECT_DELAY the item is force-claimed to the owner.  Shared (ShredderMath, ShredderResultCodes)ShredderMath.ComputeHoldDuration linearly interpolates hold time between MIN_HOLD_DURATION (1 item) and MAX_HOLD_DURATION (MAX_JUNK_COUNT items). Both client and server call it so the prompt ring and the server timing check always agree. ShredderResultCodes is a frozen enum used by both sides for unambiguous rejection reasons.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Anti-exploit thresholds are sensitive INTERACT_DISTANCE_TOLERANCE, HOLD_COMPLETION_TOLERANCE, and PER_PLAYER_COOLDOWN are the primary barriers against timing exploits and teleport-shredding. Increasing tolerances too far removes protection; tightening them too far breaks legit high-latency players.  Studio asset requirements — all three must be present or the server will warn and abort ejection:  Each workbench Model must be tagged "Workbench" with a PrimaryPart set.Each workbench must contain a child Model named "TrajectoryPoints" (tag it PlacementIgnore) with two invisible, anchored, non-collidable BasePart children: "SpawnPoint" (at the shredder output mouth) and "LandingPoint" (floor landing target).In ReplicatedStorage, a Folder named "CraftingMaterials" must contain Tool templates named "Wood" and "Metal", each with a BasePart child named "Handle". Set CanBeDropped = false on each template.  Nonce guard: the client uses a per-workbench nonce pair (holdNonce, armedNonce) to drop stale ReqShredderComplete calls when the player releases early or changes workbenches mid-hold. Modifying the hold flow must preserve this guard or the server's NO_SESSION rejection will fire spuriously.  Junk snapshot: the server snapshots junk at ReqShredderStart time. ReqShredderComplete re-filters that snapshot to tools still in the player's possession — it does not re-scan the Backpack. This prevents inflation from picking up new junk during the hold.  Energy junk exclusion: only Metal and Wood junk types are consumed and yield output. Energy junk is excluded from both the client count and the server's junk collection helpers.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: ── DROP PATH (DroppedToolService) ─────────────────────────────────────────────── Player presses Backspace → Tool drops as direct child of workspace workspace.DescendantAdded fires on IsCraftMaterial Tool handle.CollisionGroup = "DroppedMaterial" handle.CanCollide = true, Anchored = false DropLandingHelper.waitForLanding(handle) polling loop: every DROP_POLL_INTERVAL (0.1 s): GetTouchingParts → DroppableSurface contact? velocity.Magnitude < SETTLED_VELOCITY_THRESHOLD (0.5 studs/s)? → result "landed": handle.Anchored = true, rotation reset to identity (ProximityPickupServer.RegisterItem) ───────────────────────────── generate itemId (GUID) part:SetAttribute("PickupItemId", itemId) CollectionService:AddTag(part, "PickupItem") spawn invisible sphere zone (DEFAULT_RADIUS=6 studs) in workspace.PickupZones zone.Touched → player enters → executeClaimAsync() task.delay(MERGE_DELAY=1s) → _TryMerge() [same ItemType, within MERGE_RADIUS=2 studs] ──── PickupItemReady:Fire(part, itemId) ─────────────────────────────────────────► ── CLIENT (ProximityPickupController) ──────────────────────────────────────────── PickupItemReady.OnClientEvent(handle, itemId): HoverEffect.Apply(handle, HOVER_HEIGHT, HOVER_DURATION, { FloorOffset, SpinDuration }) AncestryChanged → cleanupItem on destroy ── CLAIM (zone.Touched or ProximityPickupServer.Claim) searchDocs.title: Client / Server / Shared​
searchDocs.content: Client (ProximityPickupController.client.luau)Listens to two packets only; creates no UI and does no proximity math. PickupItemReady applies a HoverEffect (bob + Y-spin) to the handle via a Janitor-managed cleanup handle, and wires AncestryChanged so the effect stops cleanly when the part is destroyed. PickupItemClaimed stops the hover effect, then for the local claimer plays a pickup SFX (via SoundManager.PlaySFXAt using CharacterAnchor to resolve the player's position) and tweens the handle toward the camera using MotionMaster.Play; for all other clients it destroys the handle immediately.  Server (ProximityPickupServer.luau)RegisterItem(part, metadata, callback, keepModel?) is the sole public registration entry. It generates a GUID itemId, tags the part "PickupItem", creates an invisible anchored sphere zone in workspace.PickupZones, and fires PickupItemReady to all clients. zone.Touched is the primary claim trigger (any player, shared-loot semantics). Claim(part, player) is the programmatic path used by the shredder's auto-collect loop. Both paths call the same executeClaimAsync which transitions the record to "Claimed", destroys the zone, broadcasts PickupItemClaimed, then after FLOAT_DURATION calls the callback and cleans up. _TryMerge runs after MERGE_DELAY and absorbs a newly registered handle into a nearby same-type unclaimed survivor, accumulating Quantity on the survivor.  Dropped-tool server (DroppedToolService.server.luau)Bootstraps two PhysicsService collision groups: DroppedMaterial (Tools that leave the player's hand) and DroppableSurface (tagged geometry). DroppedMaterial is set non-collidable with Default and collidable with DroppableSurface so dropped items fall through characters and walls but land on tagged floors. A workspace.DescendantAdded listener catches craft-material Tools parented directly to workspace (the Roblox default Backspace drop path) and delegates to DropLandingHelper.waitForLanding, which polls GetTouchingParts plus velocity until the handle settles on a DroppableSurface. Landing triggers RegisterItem with keepModel = true (the Tool itself is the inventory object, not a clone).  Shared (ProximityPickupConfig.luau)All tunable constants for radius, animation durations, merge behaviour, and the landing poll cadence.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Shared loot — not owner-only Any player who steps into the pickup sphere claims the item, regardless of who dropped it or who the shredder owner was. The auto-collect timer (AUTO_COLLECT_DELAY in ShredderConfig, 45 s) returns unclaimed floor materials to the owner via ProximityPickupServer.Claim. If owner-only pickup is ever needed, the RegisterItem signature must be extended with an owner: Player? parameter and the zone.Touched handler must gate on it (see audit comment PP6 in ProximityPickupServer).  DroppableSurface tagging — no code change needed. Any BasePart tagged "DroppableSurface" in CollectionService is automatically assigned the DroppableSurface collision group at runtime via GetInstanceAddedSignal. To make a new floor or shelf surface catchable, tag it in Studio only.  Collision groups are registered in one place. CollisionGroups.luau (ServerStorage/SharedModules) is the sole registrar and owns the full collidability matrix. Besides DroppedMaterial/DroppableSurface, it defines Character (every character BasePart, assigned by CharacterCollisionService) and WeaponProjectile (thrown charges, assigned by ServerProjectile). Because characters now live in their own group rather than Default, dropped materials and projectiles both pass through players while still colliding with world geometry. Any system that needs a new group or a new pair rule should edit CollisionGroups.luau, not call PhysicsService directly.  keepModel semantics: when keepModel = true (the DroppedToolService path), the registered part is the actual Tool that will go into the player's Backpack — RegisterItem will not destroy it. The callback sets tool.Parent = player.Backpack. When keepModel = false (the shredder path), the server clones the template, registers the clone, and the callback grants a fresh clone again; the floor handle is destroyed after claim.  Zone placement: pickup zones are parented to workspace.PickupZones (not to the item part). This prevents "trying to set locked parent!" physics warnings when the zone is destroyed at claim time while the item is still mid-float.  _TryMerge skips keepModel items: the merge logic will not absorb a keepModel item into another, because merging would destroy one of the actual inventory objects. Only non-keepModel handles (shredder clones) are eligible for merging.  Late-joining players: ProximityPickupServer has a Players.PlayerAdded listener that replays all currently "Unclaimed" PickupItemReady events to the new client, so items already on the floor will show their hover effect for late joiners.

searchDocs.content: Player holds Shift (or mobile toggle) │ ▼ SprintController (client) • applySprintIntent() → Packets.StaminaSprintIntent:Fire(true) ──► StaminaManager (server) • sets record.SprintIntent • runs Heartbeat drain/regen • syncs via StaminaStateSync ◄── Packets.StaminaStateSync (serverStamina, serverIsSprinting) ─── • currentStamina = serverStamina • if !serverIsSprinting → setSprinting(false) • Signals.OnStaminaValueChanged:Fire(currentStamina) ──► HUD bar (RenderStepped — every frame) • setSprinting(sprintIntent AND canSprintNow()) • humanoid.WalkSpeed = SprintSpeed / WalkSpeed • tweenFov(SprintFOV / DefaultFOV) • Signals.OnSprintToggled:Fire(isSprinting) ◄── Packets.StaminaBuffSync (infinite, regenMult, usageMult) ────── • Signals.OnStaminaBuffsChanged:Fire(...) ──► HUD / buff icons

searchDocs.content: Client (SprintController.client.luau)  Binds sprint to LeftShift and ButtonB (gamepad) via ContextActionService; a separate MobileSprintToggled signal handles the mobile toggle button.On each RenderStepped tick calls canSprintNow() (wraps SprintValidation.CanHumanoidSprint) and calls setSprinting accordingly.setSprinting sets humanoid.WalkSpeed, tweens FieldOfView via TweenPlus, and fires Signals.OnSprintToggled.WalkSpeed is set client-side only; there is no server-side speed reconciliation (see audit note S3 in the source).On StaminaStateSync: clamps received stamina, forces sprint off if the server says so, fires Signals.OnStaminaValueChanged for the HUD.On StaminaBuffSync: forwards buff state to Signals.OnStaminaBuffsChanged for UI and icon updates.Resets sprint intent on CharacterRemoving and on WindowFocusReleased.  Server (StaminaManager.luau)  Maintains a StaminaRecord per player (Stamina, IsSprinting, SprintIntent, LastSprintTime, LastSyncTime).On StaminaSprintIntent packet: immediately updates sprint state and calls syncPlayer.Heartbeat loop: clamps dt to MAX_STAMINA_STEP_DT = 0.1 s to prevent large delta spikes. Drains stamina at StaminaDrain * dt * UsageMultiplier while sprinting; regenerates at StaminaRegen * dt * RegenMultiplier after RegenDelay seconds of not sprinting.Syncs to the client when: sprint state changes, stamina hits 0 (forced stop), stamina refills to max, or periodic sync interval (STAMINA_SYNC_INTERVAL = 0.1 s) elapses while stamina is changing.Consults StaminaBuffManager each tick for buff multipliers; resyncs immediately on Signals.OnServerStaminaBuffStateChanged.StaminaManager.RestoreStamina(player, amount) is available for pickup items but has no caller yet.  Shared (SprintValidation.luau)  SprintValidation.CanHumanoidSprint(humanoid, rules) — returns false if health is 0, MoveDirection magnitude is below MinMoveDirection, the character is moving backward beyond MaxBackwardComponent, or horizontal speed is below MinHorizontalSpeed.Called on both client (canSprintNow) and server (canPlayerSprint) to keep the gate condition identical.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Sprint logic must be mirrored on both sides SprintValidation.CanHumanoidSprint is the shared gate. If you add a new sprint-blocking condition (e.g. stun), add it to SprintValidation and verify it is called by both SprintController (client) and StaminaManager (server). A condition added only to one side will cause desyncs.  WalkSpeed is client-only. The server does not validate movement speed; a cheating client can move at any speed. If movement integrity becomes necessary, add a server-side speed sanity check.STAMINA_SYNC_INTERVAL = 0.1 s (10 Hz). The server only sends a sync when stamina is actively changing. If stamina is full and the player is standing still, no sync is sent — this is intentional.MAX_STAMINA_STEP_DT = 0.1 s clamp. The server caps the Heartbeat delta so a lag spike cannot drain or regen an unrealistic amount of stamina in one tick. Do not remove this clamp.Buff state is authoritative on the server. StaminaBuffSync pushes the current multipliers to the client for display only; the client never applies buffs directly to the drain/regen calculation.StaminaManager.Initialize() must be called once. It is called by StaminaSystemLoader.server.luau; do not call it from a second script.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: Client code calls SoundManager.PlaySFX / PlaySFXAt / PlayLooped / PlayMusic / SetAmbience └─> SoundManager facade delegates to the appropriate submodule ├─ SFX.Play -> creates transient Sound in SoundService (2D one-shot) ├─ SFX.PlayAt -> Pool.Acquire(position) -> pooled part+Sound in workspace │ (Replicate=true) -> Packets.ReplicateSoundAtLocation:Fire -> server relay ├─ SFX.PlayLooped -> long-lived Sound in SoundService + LoopHandle returned ├─ Music.Play -> context playlist shuffle, gapped or crossfaded (MotionMaster volume fades) └─ Ambience.Set -> 2D bed Sounds in SoundService (MotionMaster fade in/out) Packets.ReplicateSoundAtLocation (client -> server -> other clients) └─> ReplicatedSoundService validates against ALLOWED_SOUND_IDS allowlist └─> FireClient to all players except sender └─> SFX.ConnectReplication handler -> Pool.Acquire positional playback Packets.SetMusicContext (server -> one client) └─> MusicService.SetContext(player, context) fires the packet └─> MusicDirector.client.luau resolves Combat > LowFuel > Normal └─> SoundManager.PlayMusic(context) -> Music.Play swaps/crossfades the playlist Signals.OnTrainStateChanged (client-local) └─> MusicDirector compares fuel / TrainConfig.MAX_FUEL against SoundConfig.Music.LowFuelPct └─> toggles the LowFuel context (no server involvement) SoundGroup bus hierarchy (Groups submodule): SoundService └─ Master SoundGroup ├─ SFX SoundGroup ├─ BGM SoundGroup └─ Ambience SoundGroup

searchDocs.title: Client / Server / Shared​
searchDocs.content: Client — SoundManager (facade + submodules)  SoundController.client.luau calls SoundManager.Init() once at startup. Init creates the SoundGroup bus hierarchy (via Groups.Ensure), warms the positional sound pool (via Pool.Ensure and per-asset pre-warm), connects the replication receiver (SFX.ConnectReplication), preloads all configured asset IDs via ContentProvider:PreloadAsync, and autostarts any ambience beds listed in SoundConfig.Ambience.Autostart.  After Init, any client script or tool may require(SharedModules.SoundManager) and call the facade. The submodules (Groups, Pool, SFX, Music, Ambience, VolumeSync) are internal and should not be required directly.  Client — MusicDirector.client.luau  A separate bootstrap script that owns the BGM context state machine. It holds two pieces of local state — combatContext (set by the server) and lowFuelActive (derived locally) — and resolves the active context by priority Combat > LowFuel > Normal every time either input changes, calling SoundManager.PlayMusic(context) only when the resolved context actually changes.  Server — MusicService.luau  Stateless server-side entry point for switching one player's BGM context: MusicService.SetContext(player, context) just fires Packets.SetMusicContext:FireClient(player, context). Gameplay code (combat events, outpost/enemy-camp zones) calls this directly; it holds no state of its own — the client tracks combat-vs-not and combines it with its own low-fuel detection.  Server — ReplicatedSoundService.server.luau  Listens on Packets.ReplicateSoundAtLocation.OnServerEvent. The server does not play audio itself — it acts only as a validated relay:  Per-player rate limit (MIN_INTERVAL = 0.05 s) rejects bursts.Payload shape is validated (data.SoundConfig.Id must be a string).The sound ID must be in ALLOWED_SOUND_IDS, which is built at startup from SoundConfig.GetReplicatedIds() — any SFX entry with Replicate = true is automatically included.Passes the original payload to all other connected players via FireClient.

searchDocs.title: Config knobs​
searchDocs.content: Everything audio lives in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/SoundConfig.luau.  Bus volumes (SoundConfig.GroupVolumes):  Bus	DefaultMaster	1.0 SFX	1.0 BGM	0.6 Ambience	0.5  Per-SFX definition fields (SoundConfig.Sfx):  Field	DescriptionId	Roblox asset ID string; empty string disables the entry Volume	Default playback volume (0–1) Pitch	Fixed pitch multiplier PitchRange	Two-element array {min, max}; randomises pitch per play Group	Bus name ("SFX", "BGM", "Ambience"); defaults to "SFX" Replicate	true to include in the server relay allowlist Debounce	Minimum seconds between plays of this entry (anti-spam) PoolInitial	Pre-allocated pool slots warmed at Init (positional only) PoolMax	Hard cap on the per-asset pool size (positional only)  Adding a new replicable SFX: add the entry to SoundConfig.Sfx with Replicate = true. SoundConfig.GetReplicatedIds() and ReplicatedSoundService pick it up automatically on next server start — no changes needed in the server script.  Music playlist fields (SoundConfig.Music.Playlists):  Field	DescriptionTracks	Array of asset IDs; played in Shuffle order if set, else array order Shuffle	Randomise track order each time the playlist (re)starts FadeIn	Seconds to fade a new track up from 0 at start FadeOut	Seconds to fade a track down to 0 at its end; also the crossfade overlap window when continuous GapMin / GapMax	Random silence range (seconds) between tracks; GapMax <= 0 means continuous (overlapping crossfade, no silence) Volume	Target playback volume for tracks in this playlist  SoundConfig.Music.LowFuelPct (default 0.25) is the fuel-fraction threshold below which MusicDirector activates the LowFuel context.

searchDocs.title: BGM contexts​
searchDocs.content: SoundConfig.Music.Playlists defines exactly three named playlists — Normal, Combat, LowFuel — one per BGM context. There is no generic/default playlist; Music.Play falls back to "Normal" only when called with no argument.  Normal — default context. Gapped: GapMin = 60, GapMax = 300 seconds of silence between tracks.Combat — server-driven via MusicService.SetContext(player, "Combat"). Continuous: GapMin = 0, GapMax = 0, so the next track starts before the current one ends (overlapping crossfade).LowFuel — client-derived automatically when fuel / TrainConfig.MAX_FUEL drops below SoundConfig.Music.LowFuelPct. Also continuous.  Priority when multiple conditions are true: Combat > LowFuel > Normal. MusicDirector.client.luau recomputes this on every change to either input (Packets.SetMusicContext.OnClientEvent for combat, Signals.OnTrainStateChanged for fuel) and only calls SoundManager.PlayMusic when the resolved context actually changes, so a low-fuel state during combat is suppressed without losing track when combat ends.  Driving combat from gameplay code (server-side, e.g. an event or outpost zone):  local MusicService = require(game.ServerStorage.SharedModules.MusicService) MusicService.SetContext(player, "Combat") -- on event/outpost enter MusicService.SetContext(player, "Normal") -- on event/outpost leave   MusicService.SetContext is stateless — it only fires Packets.SetMusicContext to the targeted player. All context resolution and the resulting PlayMusic call happen client-side in MusicDirector. See the Add a Sound playbook for adding tracks to a context playlist.

searchDocs.title: Volume persistence​
searchDocs.content: The four buses (Master, SFX, BGM, Ambience) persist across sessions via SettingsManager (ProfileStore-backed). UI binds to SoundManager.SetVolume(group, volume) to change and save a bus volume, and SoundManager.GetVolume(group) to read the current value. SetVolume applies the change locally (Groups.SetVolume) and schedules a debounced save (VolumeSync.RequestSave), which fires Packets.SaveVolume:Fire(group, volume) after coalescing rapid changes (e.g. a slider drag) into a single trailing send. On join, saved values are applied via Packets.SyncVolumes.OnClientEvent, which calls Groups.SetVolume directly — never SoundManager.SetVolume — so applying synced values does not re-trigger a save and create a feedback loop.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Never create ad-hoc Sound instances All Sound creation must go through SoundManager. Creating Sound instances by hand bypasses the bus groups (so volume controls have no effect), skips the positional pool (causing memory churn), and may produce sounds that persist across character reloads without a cleanup path.  SoundManager.Init() must be called before any Play* call. It is called once by SoundController.client.luau; do not call it again from other scripts.PlaySFXAt is positional — it parents a pooled BasePart at the given Vector3 in the workspace. The pool releases the part after sound.TimeLength + 0.05 seconds. Do not hold references to the part or sound after the call.PlayLooped returns a LoopHandle. The caller is responsible for calling handle:Stop() or handle:Destroy() when the sound is no longer needed. Abandoning a handle leaks a live Sound instance under SoundService.A sound entry with Replicate = true and an empty Id string ("") is excluded from the allowlist automatically by GetReplicatedIds(). The pool warm step also skips empty IDs. Fill in the asset ID when the sound is ready — no further config changes are required.The BGM and Ambience buses default to volumes below 1.0. SFX entries authored at Volume = 0.5 will be audibly louder than music at the same numeric volume because the bus multipliers differ.
