searchDocs.title: Client / Server / Shared​
searchDocs.content: Shared — TechTreeState.luau is a pure, stateless validator with no Roblox service calls — the single source of rules that both sides share. The client uses it to grey buttons and display accurate cost progress; the server uses it to authorise every request. Exported functions: newState, getNode, isUnlocked, isEligible, submitted, remaining, isComplete, and validateSubmit. validateSubmit checks node existence, unlock status, prereq, material membership, positive amount, and over-submission — it does not check whether the player physically holds the tools (that is a server-only concern layered on top). TechTreeResultCodes.luau is the companion frozen result-code enum; every packet response reason (e.g. TOO_FAR, EXCEEDS_REMAINING, ALREADY_UNLOCKED, NOTHING_TO_REFUND) is defined there and shared by both sides so string literals never appear in business logic.  Server — TechTreeService.server.luau is the sole owner of the authoritative unlocked / pools state. It handles ReqTechSubmit (proximity check → validateSubmit → tool count → consume → credit pool → auto-unlock on isComplete), ReqTechCancel (proximity check → snapshot and zero pool → eject), and ReqTechSnapshot (returns full { unlocked, pools } for late joiners). Broadcasts per-node deltas with TechNodeUpdate and fires Signals.OnNodeUnlocked on auto-unlock. Session-only: no DataStore.  Server — TechEffectsDispatcher.server.luau connects Signals.OnNodeUnlocked and dispatches on node.Effect.Type. The StatBuff handler is fully wired: it accumulates the numeric Effect.Amount onto the matching attribute of a shared ReplicatedStorage/TechTreeBuffs folder so other systems can read the running total. The FuelEfficiency handler is also fully wired: applyFuelEfficiency writes current * (1 / Multiplier) into TechTreeBuffs.FuelEfficiency, which TrainFuelManager reads as a drain multiplier. Any unknown effect type warns and no-ops, which lets future nodes be authored in config before their gameplay logic is written.  TechTreeService also publishes each unlocked node ID into a parallel ReplicatedStorage/TechTreeUnlocked folder (a BoolValue per unlocked node, named by nodeId). This folder is written by the server and read by the Workbench Crafting system for both server-side authorisation (gate check in WorkbenchService) and client-side greying (in WorkbenchGuiController). It is unforgeable from the client.  Server — MaterialEjector.luau is a general-purpose ejection mechanism with no knowledge of the tech tree. Its public API is MaterialEjector.Eject(bench, counts, config) where counts is a { [string]: number } material-to-quantity map and config carries all arc tuning constants. Internally it clones Tool Handle parts, animates each through a Catmull-Rom spline via MotionMaster.SplineMove from the bench TrajectoryPoints → SpawnPoint to a scattered position near LandingPoint, then registers each piece with ProximityPickupServer so players can collect them. Items beyond MAX_ANIMATED_EJECT_ITEMS are placed directly at the landing point without an animation. If TrajectoryPoints or its children are missing, the ejector degrades gracefully and drops pieces at the bench pivot instead of erroring.  Client — TechTreeGuiController.client.luau builds the TechTreeGui ScreenGui dynamically (one row per node, sorted by branch then tier). It opens via the bench TechPromptPart ProximityPrompt and closes via a header button. Steppers clamp chosen to min(held, TechTreeState.remaining) so the player can never queue more than they hold or more than is needed. The GUI repaints on TechNodeUpdate arrival by updating the local cache and calling refreshRow for all nodes — a node unlock can make its child eligible, so every row is checked. The Signals.OnTechTreeStateChanged signal is fired after each repaint for any other client code that needs to react. The server is always truth; the client never mutates cache directly except via received packets.

searchDocs.title: Studio setup​
searchDocs.content: One Model tagged TechTreeBench with its PrimaryPart set. It requires three children:  A child Model named TrajectoryPoints (tagged PlacementIgnore) holding two BasePart children: SpawnPoint (the output mouth of the bench, arc start) and LandingPoint (the floor drop zone, arc end).A child BasePart named TechPromptPart holding a ProximityPrompt — triggers the GUI open/close. The prompt's MaxActivationDistance is set to TechTreeConfig.INTERACT_DISTANCE by the client controller at runtime.ReplicatedStorage/CraftingMaterials (not a bench child) must contain Wood and Metal Tool templates with IsCraftMaterial = true and ItemType attributes set. These are shared with the Shredder.

searchDocs.title: Config knobs​
searchDocs.content: All constants live in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/TechTreeConfig.luau.  Field	Default	EffectBENCH_TAG	"TechTreeBench"	CollectionService tag on the bench Model INTERACT_DISTANCE	12	Studs within which the GUI opens / submits are accepted INTERACT_DISTANCE_TOLERANCE	5	Server-side slack added to the distance check TRAJECTORY_MODEL_NAME	"TrajectoryPoints"	Child Model holding the refund-arc endpoints SPAWN_POINT_NAME	"SpawnPoint"	Arc start (output mouth) BasePart name LANDING_POINT_NAME	"LandingPoint"	Arc end (floor) BasePart name PROMPT_PART_NAME	"TechPromptPart"	Child BasePart holding the open-GUI ProximityPrompt MATERIALS_FOLDER	"CraftingMaterials"	ReplicatedStorage folder of Wood/Metal Tool templates DROPPED_FOLDER_NAME	"DroppedMaterials"	Workspace folder for refunded pieces (reuses Shredder's) ARC_DURATION	0.55	Seconds per refunded-piece arc ARC_HEIGHT_BOOST	5	Extra arc apex height (studs) LANDING_SCATTER_RADIUS	1.5	Random landing spread around LandingPoint ITEM_EJECT_DELAY	0.06	Stagger between animated ejected pieces MAX_ANIMATED_EJECT_ITEMS	60	Cap on animated pieces; beyond this, direct-grant DIRECT_GRANT_BATCH_SIZE	25	Batch size for the non-animated overflow path AUTO_COLLECT_DELAY	45	Seconds before un-collected refund pile auto-collects  The Nodes table defines each researchable upgrade. Each node has Branch (string grouping), Tier (number, controls prereq chain), DisplayName, Description, Cost (material type → amount, e.g. { Metal = 25 }), Prereq (prior-tier node ID or nil at T1), and Effect ({ Type: string, ... }). The shipped example nodes are Durability_T1 ("Scrap Plating", StatBuff MaxHP +50, cost Metal 25) and Durability_T2 ("Iron Barricades", StatBuff MaxHP +150, cost Metal 100, prereq Durability_T1) — both fully wired through TechEffectsDispatcher. The MaxHP attribute name is kept as-is; its consumer is TrainShieldManager, which reads it as additive shield capacity: maxShield = (BASE_SHIELD + TechTreeBuffs.MaxHP) * (1 + TrainShieldBonus). See Train Shield. Fuel_T1 ("Combustion Engine", FuelEfficiency multiplier, cost Metal 80 + Wood 10) is now fully wired: TechEffectsDispatcher.applyFuelEfficiency writes a drain multiplier (current * (1 / Multiplier)) into TechTreeBuffs.FuelEfficiency, which TrainFuelManager reads on every drain tick.  Fuel-efficiency stacking rule: TrainFuelManager combines the Tech Tree multiplier with the Fuel Efficiency party perk multiplicatively:  effectiveRate = baseRate × max(0.1, TechTreeBuffs.FuelEfficiency × max(0.1, 1 − FuelEfficiencyBonus))   FUEL_DRAIN_FLOOR = 0.1 prevents the combined multiplier from ever reaching zero regardless of perk or node levels.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Server re-checks proximity on every request The client GUI proximity is never trusted. Both ReqTechSubmit and ReqTechCancel run isNearBench on the server using INTERACT_DISTANCE + INTERACT_DISTANCE_TOLERANCE. A player who submits via a modified client from too far away receives TOO_FAR.  Over-submission is rejected server-side validateSubmit rejects any amount that would exceed the remaining cost for that material (EXCEEDS_REMAINING). The stepper max in the UI is purely a courtesy — the server enforces the ceiling authoritatively. Submitting exactly the remaining amount is the only legal final submission.  Validate-then-consume ordering The server calls validateSubmit and countMaterial before touching the player's backpack. If either check fails, nothing is consumed. This means the player never loses tools to a rejected request.  Concurrent last-unit submit Roblox RemoteFunction.OnServerInvoke callbacks run on the same thread (no Luau parallelism here), so two simultaneous last-unit submits are serialised. The second one arrives after the first has already set unlocked[id] = true, so validateSubmit returns ALREADY_UNLOCKED and consumes nothing.  Effect idempotency The unlocked flag is set before OnNodeUnlocked fires, and unlockNode guards against double entry. This means OnNodeUnlocked fires exactly once per node per session — StatBuff cannot double-apply even if the signal had multiple listeners.  TechNodeUpdate packet shape is fixed to two materials TechNodeUpdate carries metalSubmitted and woodSubmitted as positional fields. Adding a third craft material to any node's Cost requires widening this packet to an Any material-to-count map and updating both the server broadcast helper (poolCounts) and the client OnClientEvent handler.  Cancel with an empty pool is rejected; missing geometry degrades gracefully ReqTechCancel on a node with no pool returns NOTHING_TO_REFUND and fires no arc. If the bench is missing its TrajectoryPoints model or either named part, MaterialEjector falls back to dropping pieces at the bench pivot position — it never errors the cancel.

searchDocs.content: Server (TrainFuelManager) Client (TrainClient / TrainFuelGuiController) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── Initialize(): fuelAtLastEvent = INITIAL_FUEL (80) isBraked = INITIAL_BRAKED (true) ──── TrainStateSync:Fire(fuel, rate, hasStarted = false isBraked, isStalled, serverTime) ──► currentRate = 0 (frozen until un-brake) reschedule() ← no task.delay while frozen Signals.OnTrainStateChanged:Fire(...) snap = { fuel, rate, isBraked, isStalled, serverTime } PlayerAdded: ──── TrainStateSync:FireClient(player, ...) ──────────────────────────────────► ── BRAKE TOGGLE ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── Player triggers lever ProxPromptPart prompt ──── ReqToggleBrake(lever) ──────────► validate: lever tag, proximity isBraked = !isBraked if first un-brake: hasStarted = true Signals.SetTrainStarted:Fire(true) commitEvent() snapshot fuel currentRate = rateForState() scheduleNonce++ reschedule() → task.delay(timeToEmpty) TrainStateSync:Fire(...) Signals.SetTrainState:Fire(running) ◄── (success, isBraked, code) ──────── update lever ActionText ("Stop Train" / "Resume Train") ── REFUEL ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── Player triggers engine ProxPromptPart prompt ──── ReqRefuelTrain(engine) ─────────► validate: engine tag, proximity, not full gather Energy tools, sort smallest first consume tools until MAX_FUEL if stalled & fuel > 0: clear stall commitEvent(newFuel) ◄── (success, fuelAdded, code) ──────── ── STALL / GAME OVER ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── task.delay(timeToEmpty) fires → onStall() isStalled = true commitEvent(0) ← exact 0, no float drift reschedule() → task.delay(GAME_OVER_DELAY) bar color = STALLED_COLOR task.delay(GAME_OVER_DELAY) fires → onGameOver() print("[TrainFuel] GAME OVER") (placeholder) ── CLIENT HUD LOOP ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── RunService.RenderStepped: predicted = snap.fuel - snap.rate * (serverTime_now - snap.serverTime) displayedFuel ≈ predicted (exponential smoothing, k=8) bar.Size = UDim2.new(pct, 0, 1, 0) bar color: green (running) / amber (braked) / red (stalled)

searchDocs.title: Client / Server / Shared​
searchDocs.content: Client — TrainClient.client.luauRegisters engine (TrainEngine-tagged) and lever (TrainBrakeLever-tagged) models via CollectionService. On engine Triggered it calls ReqRefuelTrain; surfaced error codes NO_ENERGY and FUEL_FULL fire Signals.RequestNotification toasts (warn / info respectively). On lever Triggered it calls ReqToggleBrake fire-and-forget — brake state replicates back via TrainStateSync. On PromptButtonHoldBegan it checks whether the player holds an Energy tool and shows a warning toast if not. Receives TrainStateSync and bridges it to Signals.OnTrainStateChanged.  Client — TrainFuelGuiController.client.luauReads the authored StarterGui.TrainFuelGui (never creates UI). Subscribes to Signals.OnTrainStateChanged to update snap. On every RenderStepped it computes predictedFuel from snap.fuel - snap.rate * elapsed and smooths displayedFuel toward it with frame-rate-independent exponential smoothing (k = 8). Sets FuelBar.Size and FuelText.Text, and colors the bar green/amber/red based on snap.isBraked / snap.isStalled.  Server — TrainFuelManager.luauInitialize() is called by TrainFuelSystemLoader.server.luau. All fuel arithmetic is algebraic: getFuel() = fuelAtLastEvent - currentRate * elapsed. commitEvent snapshots fuel under the old rate before switching, so the transition is seamless. A scheduleNonce guards task.delay callbacks — any subsequent commitEvent increments the nonce, and stale callbacks no-op when their captured nonce no longer matches. isRefueling is a boolean mutex that serializes concurrent refuel requests so two simultaneous players cannot both read the same pre-commit snapshot. On SetTrainState, JunkService is notified to adjust floating junk speed.  Shared — TrainConfig.luauSingle config table for fuel rates, tier recharge values, collision tags, and prompt names. Both client and server require it.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Frozen-start phase While hasStarted = false (before the first brake release), the drain rate is forced to 0 and no task.delay stall timer is scheduled. Any code path that reads currentRate or calls getFuel() before the first un-brake will see a frozen value — this is intentional. Do not bypass the hasStarted gate.  Game-over is a placeholder onGameOver() currently only prints to the output. No round reset, respawn, or UI is triggered. Do not ship this system without replacing the placeholder with a real mechanic.  Algebraic drift note: commitEvent captures now() once and uses it for both lastEventTime and the serverTime field broadcast in TrainStateSync. If you add any task.wait or async work between the snapshot and the broadcast, the client's extrapolation baseline will drift. Keep commitEvent synchronous.  Nonce guard: every commitEvent increments scheduleNonce. Stall and game-over task.delay callbacks capture the nonce at schedule time and return early if it has changed. Do not call reschedule directly — always go through commitEvent.  Refuel mutex (isRefueling): the mutex is a simple boolean, not a queue. A second refuel request while one is in-flight returns NO_ENERGY even if the player has tools. This is intentional to avoid double-spending; the player can try again immediately after.  Studio model requirements: the TrainEngine-tagged and TrainBrakeLever-tagged roots (each a Model or BasePart) must contain a BasePart named "ProxPromptPart" with a child ProximityPrompt. The prompt's MaxActivationDistance and the engine's ActionText are authored in Studio; only the lever's ActionText is set by script. Both client and server resolve the prompt part recursively via ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/PromptResolver, so it may be nested at any depth, not only as a direct child. The part's Studio name must match TrainConfig.PROMPT_PART_NAME.

searchDocs.title: Client / Server / Shared​
searchDocs.content: Client — TrainShieldController.client.luauReceives TrainShieldSync from the server and bridges it to Signals.OnTrainShieldChanged. Also surfaces the ShieldConsole-tagged model's ProximityPrompt so players can interact — on Triggered it calls ReqRechargeShield: on success it plays SoundManager.PlaySFX("ShieldRecharge"); NO_ENERGY and SHIELD_FULL error codes fire Signals.RequestNotification toasts (warn / info respectively).  Client — TrainShieldGuiController.client.luauReads the authored StarterGui.TrainShieldGui (never creates UI). Subscribes to Signals.OnTrainShieldChanged and updates ShieldBar.Size and ShieldText.Text on every receipt. No local prediction — the shield has no continuous drain, so snapshots are always current.  Server — TrainShieldManager.luauInitialize() is called by TrainShieldSystemLoader.server.luau. Owns the authoritative currentShield and maxShield values. Handles ReqRechargeShield.OnServerInvoke with an isRecharging boolean mutex. ApplyDamage is the single future damage sink; it is a no-op before hasStarted and after TrainGameOver.HasFired(). subscribeBuffs uses WaitForChild to attach GetAttributeChangedSignal listeners to both buff folders, and calls recomputeMax once after attach to catch any missed signals during the WaitForChild window.  Server — TrainShieldSystemLoader.server.luauThin bootstrap that calls TrainShieldManager.Initialize() once per server.  Server — EnergyToolHelper.luau (shared with fuel)GetEnergyTier(tool), GatherEnergyTools(player), ConsumeTool(player, tool) — server-only helpers shared by both TrainFuelManager and TrainShieldManager. Single source of truth for Energy tool scanning and consumption. No duplication between the two systems.  Server — ProximityValidation.luau (shared with fuel)FindPromptPart(root, partName), IsPlayerNear(player, promptPart, prompt, tolerance) — server-only helpers for console/engine proximity checks. Shared between refuel and shield recharge.  Server — TrainGameOver.luau (shared with fuel)HasFired(), Trigger(reason?), Reset() — idempotent game-over gate shared by both fuel stall and shield depletion. Trigger is a no-op if already fired; Reset clears the flag for round restart. Both systems funnel through this single module so the game-over fires exactly once regardless of which system hits zero first.  Shared — TrainConfig.luauShield knobs alongside fuel knobs. See Config knobs below.

searchDocs.title: Max formula​
searchDocs.content: maxShield = (BASE_SHIELD + TechTreeBuffs.MaxHP) * (1 + PartyPerkBuffs.TrainShieldBonus)   Tech Tree additive: each Durability node unlock accumulates onto TechTreeBuffs.MaxHP (Durability_T1 +50, Durability_T2 +150). This is added to BASE_SHIELD before the perk multiplier.Party perk multiplicative: TrainShieldBonus = 0.05 * maxLevel across all players (server-max resolution). Applied as a multiplier on top of the Tech Tree + base sum.Ratio-preserving recompute: when either buff changes, recomputeMax preserves the current fill ratio (currentShield / oldMax) and rounds to the nearest integer. A player at 60% shield before an upgrade stays at ~60% after.  See Tech Tree and Perks for the upstream buff systems.

searchDocs.title: ApplyDamage​
searchDocs.content: TrainShieldManager.ApplyDamage(amount, source?) is the single damage sink for the train shield. It is designed for future combat or hazard systems to call; no system calls it yet.  Guards (all must pass or the call is a no-op):  hasStarted must be true (pre-game freeze — shield cannot be damaged before first brake release)TrainGameOver.HasFired() must be false (no double-trigger after game over)amount must be > 0 and not NaN  The TrainCore tag (TrainConfig.CORE_TAG = "TrainCore") is reserved for the physical train model that future combat systems will tag; ApplyDamage does not read it directly — callers are expected to check that damage originated from a TrainCore-adjacent event before calling.

searchDocs.title: ShieldConsole model​
searchDocs.content: Each ShieldConsole-tagged root (a Model or BasePart) must contain:  A child BasePart named "ProxPromptPart" with a child ProximityPrompt. The prompt part is resolved recursively via ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/PromptResolver, so it may be nested at any depth. The prompt's MaxActivationDistance is authored in Studio; the server adds TrainConfig.PROXIMITY_TOLERANCE studs of slack when validating.  Tag the model with ShieldConsole via CollectionService (or the Studio Tag Editor). Multiple consoles are supported — each is registered independently by TrainShieldController.

searchDocs.title: TrainShieldGui hierarchy​
searchDocs.content: The HUD bar is an authored ScreenGui in StarterGui; TrainShieldGuiController never creates UI in code. Required hierarchy:  StarterGui TrainShieldGui (ScreenGui) MainContainer (Frame) ShieldBarContainer (Frame) ShieldBar (Frame) ← Size.X.Scale is set each update ShieldBarIconTextContainer (Frame) ShieldText (TextLabel) ← Text is set each update   Names are case-sensitive. If any of these are missing, TrainShieldGuiController will error on startup.

searchDocs.title: TrainCore tag (optional)​
searchDocs.content: Tag the train's structural model with "TrainCore" via CollectionService. Currently unused by TrainShieldManager (which exposes ApplyDamage as a callable API) but reserved for future combat systems that need to resolve which hits count as train damage.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Recharge mutex is not a queue isRecharging is a boolean, not a queue. A second recharge request while one is in-flight returns SHIELD_FULL or NO_ENERGY (whichever applies) — not a queued success. The player can try again immediately after. This matches the fuel system's isRefueling behavior.  Pre-game freeze hasStarted is false until Signals.SetTrainStarted fires (i.e. the first brake release on the fuel side). ApplyDamage is a no-op until then. This matches the fuel system's freeze behavior. Do not try to damage the shield before the train is started.  Passive regen is off by default SHIELD_REGEN_ENABLED = false and SHIELD_REGEN_PER_SEC = 0. No regen loop exists yet. To add passive regen, implement a RunService.Heartbeat-based loop in TrainShieldManager gated on SHIELD_REGEN_ENABLED. Do not add regen without also updating this page and the config map.  Game-over is a placeholder TrainGameOver.Trigger("shield depleted") currently results in a print to output. No round reset, respawn, or UI is triggered. This is the same placeholder used by the fuel system. Do not ship without replacing it with a real mechanic.  typeof guard on OnServerInvoke ReqRechargeShield.OnServerInvoke receives (player, console) where console is client-supplied. The handler runs a typeof(console) == "Instance" guard before attempting to acquire the isRecharging lock, so a malformed invocation (e.g. nil or a non-Instance) is rejected cleanly without erroring.

searchDocs.title: Client / Server / Shared​
searchDocs.content: Client — WeaponController.client.luauBootstrap that watches the local character for Tool equip/unequip events. Looks up WeaponConfig[tool.Name].Category and dispatches to the matching category handler (MeleeHandler, GunHandler, or ThrowableHandler). Creates one Janitor per equipped Tool (and one per character) so all connections clean up correctly on unequip, death, or weapon switch. Fires Signals.WeaponEquipped / Signals.WeaponUnequipped for the HUD, and Signals.RequestShootingCamera on equip/unequip to toggle the aim camera mode. Binds R to OnReload and G to OnDetonate for handlers that declare those callbacks.  Client — WeaponHandlers/MeleeHandler.luauCombo stepping: on each left-click it calls WeaponValidation.resolveComboSwing (tolerance 0) to determine the next step. If the click arrives during recovery it buffers one keyed retry via Janitor rather than dropping the input. Executes the predicted step: swing sound (SoundManager), optional AnimationTrack, local hitbox query (WeaponValidation.queryMeleeTargets) for an instant hitmarker (Signals.WeaponLocalHit), debug box draw, Signals.WeaponComboChanged, then fires payload-less ReqMeleeSwing. Client combo state is cleared on unequip.  Client — WeaponHandlers/GunHandler.luauHitscan + rocket cosmetic + ammo prediction. On activate, gates on a client-local fire-rate check and predicted magazine count (via AmmoApi), then fires ReqFireWeapon(origin, dir). Draws the shooter's own tracer (hitscan only; rocket has no local projectile). Supports semi and automatic fire. OnReload fires ReqReloadWeapon and predicts the ammo transition after the server-confirmed reload window. Authoritative ammo is reconciled via WeaponMagSync → Signals.WeaponMagChanged and AmmoPoolSync → Signals.AmmoPoolChanged.  Client — WeaponHandlers/ThrowableHandler.luauGrenade and C4. On activate, gates on the throw cooldown, plays throw sound, and fires ReqThrowProjectile(origin, dir). No local projectile cosmetic — the server-spawned instance replicates to all clients. For C4 (Detonation == "Manual"), OnDetonate fires ReqDetonate. Grenade ignores G.  Client — WeaponHandlers/TrajectoryPreview.luauClient-local green-neon ballistic arc shown while any throwable is equipped. Uses a fixed pool of reused BasePart segments updated every RenderStepped. Origin offset (SPAWN_OFFSET = 2.5) and upward aim bias match ServerProjectile / ThrowableHandler exactly so the preview arc matches the real projectile path. Purely cosmetic — no packets sent.  Client — WeaponEffectsController.client.luauConsumes replicated combat FX packets. WeaponFired: ignored for the local shooter (who already drew its own tracer); renders tracer + impact spark for other players' shots. WeaponImpact: impact spark + sound for all melee/gun hits. ExplosionAt: expanding neon sphere + sound for rocket, grenade, and C4 detonations — fires for everyone, including the shooter.  Shared — WeaponValidation.luauPure math run on both client (prediction) and server (authority):  canFire(lastFireTime, cooldown, now) — fire-rate gate.meleeHitbox(rootCFrame, range, hitboxSize) — single source of truth for the oriented swing box CFrame and size.queryMeleeTargets(rootCFrame, range, hitboxSize, ignore) — box overlap returning unique Humanoid-bearing Models.resolveComboSwing(state, combo, now, tolerance) — pure combo step resolution; shared so client and server stay in sync.resolveStep(config, step) — merges step overrides with weapon-level defaults into a ResolvedStep.applySpread(direction, spreadDegrees) — applies a random spread cone to an aim direction (cosmetic on client; server does its own authoritative ray).isWithinRange(origin, hitPos, maxDistance) — range cap check.ammoAfterShot(mag) / ammoReloadFromPool(mag, pool, magazineSize) — pure ammo transitions. ammoReloadFromPool returns (newMag, taken) where taken is the pool amount consumed.aoeFalloff(center, hitPos, radius, maxDamage) — linear AOE falloff.queryAOEModels(center, radius, ignore) — sphere overlap returning { model, humanoid, distance } for AOE application.  Server — WeaponServer.server.luauReceives all weapon packets. Per-category validation (fire-rate, ammo, origin tolerance, direction validity) before any damage or projectile spawn. Manages gun ammo initialisation on equip via WeaponState.EnsureAmmo + WeaponMagSync. On reload, waits ReloadTime, calls ammoReloadFromPool, consumes the drawn ammo from AmmoManager, then fires WeaponMagSync + AmmoPoolSync (the latter emitted by AmmoManager.ConsumeAmmo). On a successful throwable throw, the server destroys the player's matching Tool (onThrowProjectile — 1 Tool = 1 throw). Drives the FastCast2 rocket caster (rocketServerCaster) — its LengthChanged callback steps the cosmetic part, its Hit callback calls CombatService.ApplyAOE and broadcasts ExplosionAt. Handles throwable throw (onThrowProjectile) and detonate (onDetonate).  Server — CombatService.luauSingle damage router. Two primary entry points:  ApplyToModel(model, humanoid, amount, attackType, attacker, aoeVariant?) — applies damage to a resolved Model. Players route through HealthManager.ApplyDamage (keeping the HUD-tracked record correct); faction-tagged NPCs ("EnemyNPC" / "FriendlyNPC") take direct humanoid:TakeDamage. Anything without a recognized faction is ignored. Friendly-fire is enforced via Factions.canDamage: only Player↔Enemy damage lands; players never hurt players or friendly NPCs. A nil attacker is treated as environmental and bypasses the faction gate. Self-damage from one's own AOE is exempt.ApplyAOE(center, radius, maxDamage, attackType, attacker, ignore) — calls queryAOEModels, applies aoeFalloff to each target, and routes through ApplyToModel with aoeVariant = "Explosion".  Also available: ApplyToPart(part, amount, attackType, attacker, aoeVariant?) — resolves a hit part to its Humanoid-bearing Model then calls ApplyToModel.  Server — WeaponState.luauPer-player authoritative state. Fields per player record:  lastFire: { [weaponName]: number } — os.clock() of last shot/swing per weapon; gates fire-rate.combo: { [weaponName]: { index, lastHitTime } } — authoritative combo progress.ammo: { [weaponName]: { mag, reloadEndsAt } } — magazine count and reload window (reloadEndsAt is the os.clock() timestamp when a reload finishes; 0 means not reloading). Reserve is no longer stored here — pool ammo is owned by AmmoManager.active: { ActiveCharge } — active manual throwables (C4) awaiting detonation.  Key functions: EnsureAmmo (seeds magazine from config), GetMag/SetMag, GetLastFire/SetLastFire, GetCombo/SetCombo, IsReloading, SetReloadEnd, GetActiveCount, AddActive, TakeAllActive. Clear destroys all active charges and removes the player's record on PlayerRemoving.  Server — ServerProjectile.luauSpawns and owns server-authoritative, replicated projectile instances cloned from ReplicatedStorage/WeaponAssets into workspace/ServerProjectiles. Two spawn paths:  spawnRocket(templateName, cframe) — anchored, non-collidable cosmetic part; the caller (WeaponServer) steps its CFrame along the FastCast2 cast.spawnThrowable(templateName, origin, direction, speed, rest, ignore) — server-owned physics rigid body. prepareAssembly un-anchors all parts, sets the WeaponProjectile collision group (passes through characters), and applies per-mode elasticity: "Stick" (C4) elasticity = 0 (lands dead); "Bounce" (Grenade) elasticity = 0.15 (one small hop). installSettle polls until the charge has contacted a world surface and come to rest, then anchors it flat. Network ownership is kept server-side via root:SetNetworkOwner(nil).

searchDocs.title: HUD integration contract​
searchDocs.content: This system ships no UI. A HUD widget that wants to display ammo or combat feedback must consume:  Packets (server → owning client, handled by AmmoApi): WeaponMagSync(weaponName, mag) — authoritative magazine count sent on equip, after each shot, and after reload completion.AmmoPoolSync(ammoType, amount) — authoritative pool count for a given ammo type sent whenever the pool changes (shot, reload, craft). AmmoApi read surface (preferred over raw packets): AmmoApi.GetMag(weaponName) → (mag, magSize) — current magazine and max size.AmmoApi.GetPool(ammoType) → (amount, capacity) — current pool and capacity cap.AmmoApi.GetEquippedAmmo() → (mag, magSize, pool, cap)? — combined ammo for the equipped gun; nil for non-guns.AmmoApi.GetThrowableCount(toolName) → count — counts matching Tools in the Backpack + equipped slot. Signals (client-side): WeaponEquipped(toolName, category) — fired on equip.WeaponUnequipped(toolName) — fired on unequip.WeaponMagChanged(weaponName, mag) — fired by AmmoApi on predicted mag update and on WeaponMagSync reconciliation.AmmoPoolChanged(ammoType, amount) — fired by AmmoApi on AmmoPoolSync or local prediction.ThrowableCountChanged(toolName, count) — fired by AmmoApi when the backpack throwable count changes.WeaponReloadStarted(weaponName, reloadTime) — fired when a reload request is sent.WeaponReloadComplete(weaponName) — fired when the reload window elapses or reload is rejected.WeaponLocalHit(model) — fired on a predicted melee/hitscan hit for hitmarker display.WeaponComboChanged(toolName, stepIndex, totalSteps) — fired on each combo step advance.  See Signals Map for the full signal registry.

searchDocs.title: Pool and magazine model​
searchDocs.content: Ammo is split into two distinct layers:  Magazine (WeaponState, server) — per-gun in-memory count representing what is currently loaded. The magazine is seeded to MagazineSize rounds on the gun's first equip (EnsureAmmo) and then persists across deaths within the session (it is not refilled on every equip or on respawn). On each shot the magazine decrements by one. On reload, the magazine refills from the pool. The magazine is the only ammo state WeaponState owns; there is no longer a reserve field per gun.Pool (AmmoManager, server) — per-player, per-type in-memory count of unloaded ammo. Entirely session-only — nothing is persisted to a DataStore. The pool is seeded to each type's Starting value on the player's first spawn only; it then persists across deaths for the rest of the session (dying never refills reserve ammo). AmmoManager.EnsureStarting re-syncs the current pool to the owning client on each respawn so the HUD shows the correct value after the character and Backpack rebuild. The pool is shared across all guns of the same ammo type.

searchDocs.title: Reload flow​
searchDocs.content: Client fires ReqReloadWeapon.Server checks mag < magSize and pool > 0; rejects otherwise (returns 0 reload time).Server waits ReloadTime, then calls ammoReloadFromPool(mag, pool, magSize) (in WeaponValidation), which returns (newMag, taken).AmmoManager.ConsumeAmmo(player, ammoType, taken) is called atomically; it clamps, deducts, and fires AmmoPoolSync to the owning client.Server sets the new magazine via WeaponState.SetMag and fires WeaponMagSync to the owning client.

searchDocs.title: Throwables​
searchDocs.content: Throwables are physical Roblox Tools in the player's Backpack. Each throw consumes exactly one Tool: WeaponServer.onThrowProjectile destroys the equipped throwable Tool server-side on a successful throw. There is no numeric reserve or CarryCount in WeaponState — count is inferred by AmmoApi.GetThrowableCount by scanning the Backpack and equipped slot.  C4 detonation is intentionally decoupled from holding the Tool: ThrowableDetonateController.client.luau listens for the global G keybind and fires ReqDetonate regardless of what is currently equipped. The server no-ops if the player has no active charges. This design handles the edge case where the last C4 was thrown (destroying its Tool) but live charges are still stuck to surfaces awaiting detonation.

searchDocs.title: Crafting ammo​
searchDocs.content: See Workbench Crafting for the full crafting flow; the recipe values below are illustrative — WorkbenchConfig.Recipes is canonical.  Ammo can be replenished at a Workbench. Crafting recipes in the "ammo" category call AmmoManager.AddAmmo (which clamps to Capacity). Available ammo recipes:  Recipe	OutputCraftLightAmmo	+60 Light Rounds CraftHeavyAmmo	+12 Heavy Rounds CraftRocketAmmo	+2 Rockets CraftGrenade	3 Grenade Tools CraftC4	1 C4 Tool  Weapon Tool recipes clone the template from ServerStorage/WeaponTemplates directly into the player's Backpack.

searchDocs.title: Client read surface (AmmoApi)​
searchDocs.content: AmmoApi (src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/AmmoApi.luau) is the single client-side cache and read surface for all ammo data. HUD widgets and handlers should call AmmoApi rather than listening to raw packets.  Method	Returns	NotesGetMag(weaponName)	(mag, magSize)	Current magazine count and magazine capacity. GetPool(ammoType)	(amount, capacity)	Current pool count and pool capacity cap. GetEquippedAmmo()	(mag, magSize, pool, cap)?	Combined view for the equipped gun; nil for non-guns or unarmed. GetThrowableCount(toolName)	count	Counts matching Tool instances in Backpack + equipped slot.  AmmoApi listens to WeaponMagSync and AmmoPoolSync packets, updates its cache, and fires the corresponding Signals. It also watches the player's Backpack for tool additions/removals (rebinding per-character via Janitor) to keep GetThrowableCount accurate. Bootstrapped once by AmmoController.client.luau.

searchDocs.title: Config knobs​
searchDocs.content: WeaponConfig.luau is the per-weapon registry. Edit stats here — never in handler or server code.  Common fields (all weapons):  Category — "Melee" | "Gun" | "Throwable".DisplayName — human-readable label.ToolName — must match the in-game Tool's Name exactly (used as a packet/state key).Damage — base damage per hit (melee: default per-step; gun: per bullet; throwable: 0, AOE only).DamageType — "Melee" | "Bullet" | "AOE".HeadshotMultiplier? — optional multiplier applied by the server when the ray hits a part named "Head" (gun only).  Melee fields:  Range — forward reach in studs (also hitbox depth).HitboxSize — Vector3 width × height (Z ignored; depth = Range).SwingSound / ImpactSound — SoundConfig.Sfx keys.SwingAnimId? — optional rbxassetid for a swing animation track.Combos — map keyed by input ("Primary" = left-click; "Secondary" reserved). Each ComboDef has: Steps[] — ordered ComboStep array; combo length = #Steps. Each step: Recovery (min seconds before next hit), ChainWindow (seconds to keep combo alive past this hit), optional overrides Damage?, Range?, HitboxSize?, AnimId?, SwingSound?, ImpactSound?.ResetCooldown — brief lockout after the finisher before restarting at hit 1.  Gun fields:  FireMode — "Hitscan" | "Projectile".RPM — rounds per minute; fire interval = 60 / RPM.Automatic — true = hold-to-fire; false = semi-auto.MagazineSize — rounds loaded per magazine. Reserve pool is not stored here; it is owned by AmmoManager and keyed by AmmoType.AmmoType — ammo-pool key ("Light" | "Heavy" | "Rocket"); maps this gun to its shared pool in AmmoConfig.ReloadTime — seconds.Spread — max cone half-angle in degrees.MaxDistance — hit range cap (studs).FireSound / ReloadSound / DrySound / ImpactSound — SoundConfig.Sfx keys.Projectile-only additions: ProjectileSpeed (studs/sec), Gravity (Vector3 acceleration), AOERadius, AOEDamage (center damage, linear falloff to 0 at radius), CosmeticTemplate (name in ReplicatedStorage/WeaponAssets).  Throwable fields:  Detonation — "Fuse" (auto after FuseTime) | "Manual" (all charges detonate on ReqDetonate).Rest — "Bounce" (small hop, settles) | "Stick" (lands dead on first contact).ThrowSpeed — initial velocity (studs/sec).FuseTime — (Fuse only) seconds from throw to detonation.MaxActive — (Manual only) max simultaneously active charges per player.AOERadius / AOEDamage — explosion radius and center damage (linear falloff).CooldownTime — seconds between throws.CosmeticTemplate — name in ReplicatedStorage/WeaponAssets.ThrowSound / ExplodeSound — SoundConfig.Sfx keys.  Note: CarryCount has been removed. How many throwables a player carries is determined by how many matching Tool instances are in their Backpack (crafted or spawned). AmmoApi.GetThrowableCount reads this count at runtime.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas / anti-exploit​
searchDocs.content: Fire-rate enforcement Guns enforce 60/RPM intervals via WeaponState.GetLastFire; melee enforces Recovery, ChainWindow, and ResetCooldown per combo step via WeaponValidation.resolveComboSwing (server tolerance = 0.05 s). Requests that arrive too early are silently dropped.  Server-authoritative ammo and reload Magazine counts and reload timing are owned by WeaponState on the server; pool ammo is owned by AmmoManager. Firing at an empty magazine is rejected. Firing while a reload window is active (reloadEndsAt > now) is rejected. Reloading with an empty pool is rejected. Neither the magazine count, pool count, nor the reload timer is read from the client.  Origin, spread, and distance validation The claimed muzzle origin for guns and throw origin for throwables must be within 14 studs of the server-side HumanoidRootPart position and must be a finite (non-NaN) vector. Claimed directions with zero or non-finite magnitude are rejected before normalization. The server caps hitscan range at MaxDistance on its authoritative ray; applySpread is applied client-side for feel only — the server recasts from the validated origin and does not verify the spread angle.  Friendly-fire prevention Enforced in CombatService.ApplyToModel via Factions.canDamage. Only Player↔Enemy damage lands. Players never damage other players or friendly NPCs; enemies never damage other enemies or friendly NPCs. Self-damage from one's own AOE is exempt — the self-check bypasses the faction gate so a player's own rocket can still hurt them if they walk into the blast.  NPC pass-through via CollectionService tag: the "EnemyNPC" / "FriendlyNPC" CollectionService tag is the dual-purpose NPC marker. It gates damage routing in CombatService (only tagged NPCs with a Humanoid take weapon damage) and, via NpcCollisionService, places NPC parts in the Character collision group so thrown charges physically pass through them. A Model without a recognized faction tag receives no damage and does not block thrown projectiles — tag it or it is invisible to the weapon system.  HealthManager routing via CombatService: HealthManager writes record.Health → humanoid.Health but never reads back from the Humanoid. Any external write that bypasses HealthManager.ApplyDamage (via CombatService) will leave the HUD showing a stale record value. Never write to humanoid.Health directly for player damage.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: Client (WorkbenchGuiController) Server (WorkbenchService) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── ── OPEN ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── Player walks within INTERACT_DISTANCE ProximityPrompt fires (CraftPromptPart) GUI opens; recipe grid populated from WorkbenchConfig.Recipes TechTreeUnlocked folder checked → grey any gated recipe whose RequiresNode value is not yet in the folder ── SELECT RECIPE ──────────────────────────────────────────────────── Player clicks a recipe tile Detail panel shows DisplayName, Description, Tier badge, Cost rows (Wood / Metal — exactly two rows max), RequiresNode note ── CRAFT ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── Player clicks Craft button ──── ReqCraft(bench: Instance, recipeId: String) ─────────────► Server (WorkbenchService) validates, in order: look up recipe in WorkbenchConfig (else UNKNOWN_RECIPE) verify bench is a tagged Workbench Model (else INVALID_TARGET) re-check proximity (INTERACT_DISTANCE + INTERACT_DISTANCE_TOLERANCE) (else TOO_FAR) CRAFT_COOLDOWN gate (per-player timestamp) (else COOLDOWN) check RequiresNode gate in TechTreeUnlocked (else LOCKED) CraftOutputDispatcher.isFeasible(recipe.Output) → verify output slot is usable BEFORE consuming any materials (else OUTPUT_FAILED) player holds enough cost materials (else INSUFFICIENT_MATERIALS) on pass: consume materials from player Backpack, then CraftOutputDispatcher.grant(player, recipe.Output) Kind == "Weapon" → clone from WeaponTemplates Kind == "Armor" → ArmorManager.SetTier(player, output.Tier) Kind == "Placeable" → grant PlaceableTools Tool record cooldown timestamp ◄── (success: Boolean8, code: NumberU8) ────────────────────────── if success: Signals.OnItemCrafted:Fire(recipeId) GUI shows success FX / SoundManager.PlaySFX(CraftSuccess) else: show failure toast / SoundManager.PlaySFX(CraftFail)

searchDocs.title: Client / Server / Shared​
searchDocs.content: Shared — WorkbenchResultCodes.luau (ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/) is a frozen result-code enum identical in role to TechTreeResultCodes. Every reject reason (NONE, UNKNOWN_RECIPE, INVALID_TARGET, TOO_FAR, COOLDOWN, LOCKED, OUTPUT_FAILED, INSUFFICIENT_MATERIALS) is defined here so neither side ever uses bare string literals in business logic.  Shared — Configs/WorkbenchConfig.luau (ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/) is the single tuning surface: interaction constants, output template folder names, category lists, sound keys, and the Recipes table. See Config knobs below.  Shared — WorkbenchValidation.luau (ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/) is a pure, stateless validator with no Roblox service calls. It runs on both client (button-greying, cost display) and server (authority). Exported functions mirror the pattern from TechTreeState: recipe existence, gate check, material sufficiency.  Server — WorkbenchService.server.luau (ServerScriptService/) is the sole owner of the authoritative ReqCraft handler. It resolves the bench instance, re-checks proximity, runs WorkbenchValidation, calls CraftOutputDispatcher.isFeasible before touching any materials, then consumes materials and calls CraftOutputDispatcher.grant. Manages the per-player cooldown timestamp.  Server — CraftOutputDispatcher.luau (ServerStorage/SharedModules/) handles the three output kinds:  Kind == "Weapon" — clones the named Tool from ServerStorage/WeaponTemplates into the player's Backpack.Kind == "Armor" — calls ArmorManager.SetTier(player, output.Tier), updating ArmorState/<UserId>.ArmorBaseReduction in ReplicatedStorage.Kind == "Placeable" — grants the named Tool from ReplicatedStorage/PlaceableTools/<Name> into the player's Backpack.  isFeasible(output) verifies the target output slot is usable (e.g. the template exists, the tier is valid) before materials are consumed. A misconfigured recipe never costs the player materials.  Client — WorkbenchGuiController.client.luau (StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/) opens via the bench CraftPromptPart ProximityPrompt. Builds the recipe grid from WorkbenchConfig.Recipes and greys any recipe whose RequiresNode is not present in ReplicatedStorage/TechTreeUnlocked. Fires ReqCraft on the Craft button and fires Signals.OnItemCrafted on a confirmed success. The CloseButton closes the GUI. The DropdownButton is driven by the reusable Dropdown widget, which fires Signals.RequestWorkbenchCategory on selection to re-filter the grid. Uses a Janitor per GUI open/close lifecycle.

searchDocs.title: Recipe schema​
searchDocs.content: Recipes are declared in WorkbenchConfig.Recipes as a { [string]: Recipe } table keyed by a string recipe ID.  export type Output = { Kind: "Weapon", ToolName: string } | { Kind: "Armor", Tier: number } | { Kind: "Placeable", PlaceableName: string } export type Recipe = { Category: string, -- one of RecipeCategories ("weapons"|"ammo"|"armor"|"workstation") DisplayName: string, Description: string, Tier: number, -- 1..5 flavor/quality badge only; NOT a prerequisite ladder Icon: string, -- rbxassetid:// string for the grid tile and detail panel Cost: { Wood: number?, Metal: number? }, RequiresNode: string?, -- TechTree nodeId gate; nil = always available Output: Output, }   Tier is a purely cosmetic quality badge displayed as a star rating in the GUI. It has no prerequisite chain and imposes no unlock order — any recipe with RequiresNode = nil is available to craft at any time regardless of Tier. The only unlock gate is RequiresNode.  The Cost table is limited to Wood and Metal because the GUI renders exactly two material rows. Adding a third material requires a GUI layout change and a matching config key.

searchDocs.title: Tech-Tree gate seam​
searchDocs.content: TechTreeService publishes unlocked node IDs into a ReplicatedStorage/TechTreeUnlocked folder (a BoolValue per unlocked node, named by nodeId) in parallel to the existing TechTreeBuffs folder. This folder is written by the server when a node unlocks and is read by:  WorkbenchService (server): authoritative gate check. A craft request whose recipe has a non-nil RequiresNode is rejected with LOCKED if the corresponding BoolValue is absent or false. Because the folder is written by the server, clients cannot forge an unlock.WorkbenchGuiController (client): greying. Recipes with a locked RequiresNode are rendered as unavailable in the grid so players know they need to unlock the tech node first. The client reads this folder but never writes it.  See Tech Tree for the full TechTreeService data flow and the TechTreeBuffs folder contract.

searchDocs.title: Studio setup​
searchDocs.content: Tag the Workbench Model. In ReplicatedStorage/PlaceableItems/Workbench, tag the root Model with the CollectionService tag Workbench (the same tag the Shredder scans for — one Model serves as both crafting station and shredder). Give it a BasePart named CraftPromptPart (anywhere under the Model — PromptResolver finds it recursively) containing a ProximityPrompt. Set the Model's PrimaryPart. The shredder half uses a sibling ShredPromptPart. Create ServerStorage/WeaponTemplates. Add a folder named WeaponTemplates inside ServerStorage. Place craftable weapon Tools here (e.g. clones of Pistol and SMG from StarterPack). These are separate from the StarterPack copies — the Workbench clones from here into the player's Backpack, so stat changes or visual differences can live here independently. Ensure craftable placeables exist. Each recipe with Output.Kind == "Placeable" needs a Tool at ReplicatedStorage/PlaceableTools/<PlaceableName>. The Workbench itself already follows this convention as a grid-placeable item. Material templates are shared. ReplicatedStorage/CraftingMaterials already holds Wood and Metal Tool templates (shared with the Shredder and Tech Tree systems). No duplication is needed. Wire TechTreeUnlocked. TechTreeService creates and writes this folder automatically at runtime. No manual Studio setup is required for the gate to function. If testing in isolation (without a running TechTreeService), create a Folder named TechTreeUnlocked in ReplicatedStorage and add BoolValue children named after whichever node IDs you want to treat as unlocked.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas / anti-exploit​
searchDocs.content: Server re-checks proximity on every craft The client proximity prompt is never trusted. WorkbenchService re-runs the distance check using INTERACT_DISTANCE + INTERACT_DISTANCE_TOLERANCE on every ReqCraft call. A player exploiting from range receives TOO_FAR.  Feasibility is checked before materials are consumed CraftOutputDispatcher.isFeasible(recipe.Output) runs (and must succeed) before any material Tool is removed from the player's Backpack. A recipe that references a missing weapon template or an invalid armor tier therefore fails without costing the player anything. Misconfigured recipes are safe to ship; they only result in a visible craft failure.  Tech-Tree gate is read from server-written state The TechTreeUnlocked folder is written exclusively by TechTreeService on the server. A client cannot create or modify entries in that folder. The server re-reads the folder on every ReqCraft call, so a client that somehow fakes the UI greying cannot bypass the gate.  Cost is limited to Wood and Metal The GUI renders exactly two material rows. Cost may only specify Wood and/or Metal. Adding a third material type (e.g. Energy) requires a GUI layout change alongside the config key — otherwise the cost is silently unchecked on the client (though the server will still validate it).  Tier is a flavor badge, not a prerequisite ladder Tier (1–5) drives the star-rating display only. There is no inter-recipe prerequisite chain derived from Tier values. The sole unlock gate is RequiresNode. Do not attempt to use Tier as a crafting order enforcer — it will not work without code changes.  Known edge case: respawn mid-craft (v1) If a player's Backpack disappears between the feasibility check passing and CraftOutputDispatcher.grant executing (e.g. the player respawns during that narrow window), materials may be consumed but the grant returns OUTPUT_FAILED. The client receives a failure response and the player loses the materials. This is an accepted v1 limitation — the window is sub-frame in practice. A future refund path or a pre-grant Backpack re-check is the recommended fix.
